rxn03918.other_comments: This is the HldE kinase reaction (D-glycero-beta-D-manno-heptose 7-phosphate kinase) in the ADP-L-glycero-D-manno-heptose biosynthesis pathway for LPS inner core. ATP phosphorylates the 1-position of D-glycero-D-manno-heptose 7-phosphate to form the 1,7-bisphosphate, producing ADP and a proton. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: ATP + heptose-7-P yields ADP + H+ + heptose-1,7-bisP. The phosphoryl transfer with ATP hydrolysis drives the reaction essentially irreversibly forward in vivo.

rxn00038.other_comments: This is the hydrolysis of a dimeric ester of (R)-3-hydroxybutanoate (a poly-3-hydroxybutyrate breakdown intermediate). One water cleaves the ester bond, yielding 2 molecules of (R)-3-hydroxybutanoate. Atom and charge balance: the substrate dimer carries one carboxylate (-1); hydrolysis produces two carboxylates (-2 total) plus one H+ (+1), giving net -1, matching the left side. Carbon: 8 (dimer) = 2 x 4. Stoichiometry and mass/charge are balanced.

rxn10776.other_comments: This is the MurG-catalyzed reaction (GlcNAc transferase) in bacterial peptidoglycan biosynthesis, transferring N-acetylglucosamine from UDP-GlcNAc to lipid I (undecaprenyl-pyrophosphoryl-MurNAc-pentapeptide) to form lipid II, releasing UDP. Here the muramoyl moiety is the N-glycolyl variant (common in Mycobacteria). The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: a GlcNAc residue is transferred from UDP-GlcNAc to the lipid intermediate, producing UDP and the GlcNAc-bearing lipid II analog. Atoms balance as written.

rxn09909.other_comments: This represents an ATP-dependent dipeptide ligase (L-amino acid ligase, Lal type) forming the dipeptide Ala-Met from L-alanine and L-methionine. Mass and charge balance: ATP + Ala + Met -> ADP + Pi + H+ + dipeptide. The peptide bond formation releases one water, but the hydrolysis of ATP to ADP + Pi consumes one water, so the net water cancels and atoms balance. Charge is balanced (ATP -4 + Ala 0 + Met 0 = -4 on left; ADP -3 + Pi -2 + H+ +1 + dipeptide 0 = -4 on right). The reaction is stoichiometrically correct.

rxn13771.other_comments: This represents an NADH oxidase reaction reducing molecular oxygen to water while oxidizing NADH to NAD+. rxn13316.other_comments: This is a transport reaction moving isoamyl alcohol (3-methyl-1-butanol) across a membrane between two compartments (e.g., extracellular and cytosol). rxn04476.other_comments: This is a SAM-dependent C-methyltransferase reaction (TylC3/EryBIII-type) in deoxysugar biosynthesis. SAM donates a methyl group to the C-3 amino sugar substrate (dTDP-3-amino-2,3,6-trideoxy-D-threo-hexopyranos-4-ulose), producing the C-methylated product, S-adenosyl-homocysteine (SAH), and a proton. The atoms balance: a methyl group is transferred from SAM, converting it to SAH, with one H+ released. Note the stereochemical change from D-threo to D-erythro reflects the new quaternary/methylated center.

rxn03072.other_comments: This reaction describes the oxidative ring-opening/dehydrogenation interconversion between 3-hydroxy-L-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (a cyclic Schiff base/imine form) and 4-hydroxy-L-glutamate (4-hydroxyglutamate, the open-chain amino acid). The cyclic pyrroline-5-carboxylate spontaneously equilibrates with its open-chain glutamate-semialdehyde form; here the imine carbon is oxidized by NADP+ with water acting as the oxygen/hydration source, yielding the carboxylate. Stoichiometry: counting C5 backbone is conserved (both are C5 with one OH and the ring N becoming the alpha-amino group). Hydrogen and charge balance is plausible: addition of one H2O across the C=N bond plus NADP+ oxidation generates NADPH + H+. One H2O appears stoichiometrically excessive (the second water may not be balanced), but the net redox logic is sound. This is analogous to delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase chemistry on a hydroxylated substrate.

rxn02807.other_comments: This is a flavin-dependent monooxygenase (hydroxylase) reaction. 2,4-dichlorophenol is hydroxylated at the 6-position using O2 (one atom incorporated into substrate forming the catechol, the other reduced to water), with NADPH as the electron donor. The product 3,5-dichlorocatechol is consistent with hydroxylation ortho to the existing hydroxyl. Atoms balance: C6H4Cl2O (substrate) + O2 + NADPH + H+ -> C6H4Cl2O2 (dichlorocatechol) + H2O + NADP+. Charges and H balance appropriately.

rxn01852.other_comments: This is a toluene side-chain monooxygenase reaction. Toluol (toluene) is hydroxylated on its methyl group to form Phenylcarbinol (benzyl alcohol). rxn04779.other_comments: This is a hydrolytic deamination of cyromazine (a melamine derivative) where an amino group is replaced by a hydroxyl group, releasing ammonia. Such hydrolytic deaminations are essentially irreversible in vivo, proceeding in the forward (hydrolysis) direction.

rxn02938.other_comments: This is the reaction catalyzed by N5-CAIR mutase / PurE class enzymes (phosphoribosylaminoimidazole carboxylase). Stoichiometry balances: CAIR has the extra carboxylate that becomes CO2, and AIR is the decarboxylated product. rxn10900.other_comments: This is D-lactate dehydrogenase (menaquinone-linked), oxidizing D-lactate to pyruvate while reducing menaquinone-6 to menaquinol-6. Stoichiometry is balanced (1:1:1:1) assuming the menaquinone/menaquinol pair correctly accounts for the 2H. In vivo this respiratory dehydrogenase feeds electrons into the menaquinone pool and operates in the direction of lactate oxidation.

rxn06195.other_comments: This is the protein-glutamate O-methyltransferase reaction (EC 2.1.1.80), involved in bacterial chemotaxis methyl-accepting protein modification. SAM donates a methyl group to a protein glutamate residue, forming the glutamate methyl ester and S-adenosyl-homocysteine (SAH). The reaction is stoichiometrically balanced (one methyl group transferred). SAM-dependent methyltransferases are thermodynamically favorable in the forward (methylation) direction in vivo due to the high group transfer potential of SAM and rapid removal of SAH.

rxn05366.other_comments: This is an enoyl-ACP reductase reaction in fatty acid biosynthesis (branched-chain/methyl-branched fatty acid elongation). NADPH reduces the trans-2 double bond of the 6-methyl-oct-2-enoyl-ACP to yield the saturated 6-methyl-octanoyl-ACP. Stoichiometry is balanced: the C=C double bond is reduced by addition of two H atoms (one hydride from NADPH, one proton from H+), consuming NADPH + H+ and producing NADP+.

rxn03959.other_comments: This is the reaction catalyzed by 2-(R)-hydroxypropyl-CoM dehydrogenase (also known as 2-hydroxypropyl-CoM dehydrogenase), part of the bacterial epoxide/alkene metabolism pathway in organisms such as Xanthobacter autotrophicus. It oxidizes the secondary alcohol of 2-(R)-hydroxypropyl-CoM to the corresponding ketone (2-oxopropyl-CoM, also called 2-ketopropyl-CoM), reducing NAD+ to NADH. The reaction is balanced: the carbon, hydrogen, sulfur, and charge balance with one hydride transferred to NAD+ and one proton released. As an NAD-dependent alcohol/ketone oxidoreductase, it is thermodynamically reversible, though in the propylene catabolic pathway it proceeds in the oxidative (forward) direction.

rxn07875.other_comments: This is an NAD-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase reaction converting geranial (an aldehyde) to geranic acid (carboxylic acid). The stoichiometry is balanced: the aldehyde (RCHO) plus water plus NAD+ yields the carboxylic acid (RCOOH) plus NADH plus 2 H+. Atom and charge balance hold: water provides the additional oxygen, two hydrogens are released (one to NADH as hydride, the other as proton), giving 2 H+ on the product side. Aldehyde oxidation by NAD-dependent dehydrogenases is essentially irreversible in vivo, strongly favoring carboxylic acid formation.

rxn12746.other_comments: This is the 6-hydroxynicotinate 3-monooxygenase reaction (EC 1.14.13.114), a flavin-dependent monooxygenase that hydroxylates 6-hydroxynicotinate with concomitant decarboxylation to yield 2,5-dihydroxypyridine. As a monooxygenase consuming NADH and O2 with irreversible decarboxylation, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction in vivo.

rxn02696.other_comments: This is a beta-glucan glucohydrolase (exo-cellulase/beta-glucosidase-type) reaction. rxn01022.other_comments: This is the MTA phosphorylase (MTAP) reaction, EC 2.4.2.28. It phosphorolytically cleaves 5'-deoxy-5'-methylthioadenosine (MTA) into adenine and 5-methylthio-alpha-D-ribose-1-phosphate. The stoichiometry is balanced: MTA + phosphate yields adenine + S-methyl-5-thio-D-ribose-1-phosphate. In vivo the reaction proceeds in the direction of MTA salvage (cleavage), driven by removal/recycling of products in the methionine salvage pathway.

rxn04334.other_comments: This reaction represents the NADPH-dependent reduction of 5-oxoavermectin '1a' aglycone (5-keto) to avermectin B1a aglycone (5-hydroxy). A ketone is reduced to a secondary alcohol, consuming NADPH + H+ and producing NADP+. rxn02113.other_comments: This is the alpha-acetolactate decarboxylase reaction (EC 4.1.1.5). ALCTT (2-acetolactate, i.e. 2-hydroxy-2-methyl-3-oxobutanoate) is decarboxylated to ACTN (acetoin) with release of CO2, consuming a proton. The stoichiometry is balanced: 2-acetolactate (C5H7O4-) + H+ yields CO2 + acetoin (C4H8O2). Decarboxylations are essentially irreversible in vivo due to release of CO2.

rxn02192.other_comments: This reaction represents the action of leukotriene A4 hydrolase (LTA4H), which converts the unstable epoxide leukotriene A4 (LTA4) into leukotriene B4 (LTB4) via hydrolytic ring opening with addition of water. The stoichiometry H2O + LTA4 -> LTB4 is balanced, as the epoxide is hydrolyzed and the oxygen from water is incorporated to yield a dihydroxy product. The (5S,6S)-5,6-epoxyicosatetraenoate description corresponds to LTA4. rxn11606.other_comments: This is a SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase reaction. The methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine is transferred to the 4-hydroxyl group of N-benzoyl-4-hydroxyanthranilate, producing the 4-methoxy product and S-adenosyl-homocysteine plus a proton. Atom balance is consistent: SAM donates CH3 (becoming SAH), and the hydroxyl oxygen becomes the methoxy oxygen with release of H+. Stoichiometry is balanced.

rxn02899.other_comments: This is a cis-dihydrodiol dehydrogenase reaction in the bacterial phenanthrene degradation pathway. The (+)-cis-3,4-dihydrophenanthrene-3,4-diol is oxidized by NAD+ to form the aromatic catechol product phenanthrene-3,4-diol, with reduction of NAD+ to NADH and release of a proton. The reaction is balanced: the substrate dihydrodiol loses two hydrogens (2H = NADH + H+) to rearomatize into the catechol. Atom and charge balance are consistent.

rxn12196.other_comments: This represents malate dehydrogenase (quinone), EC 1.1.5.4, oxidizing L-malate to oxaloacetate while reducing a quinone (Q) to quinol (QH2). The reaction is balanced: L-malate is oxidized losing 2H (2 electrons + 2 protons), and the quinone accepts 2H to become quinol. Stoichiometry is correct as written. In vivo, coupling to the quinone pool (high redox potential acceptor) drives the otherwise unfavorable malate-to-oxaloacetate oxidation forward.

rxn01645.other_comments: This is the L-2,4-diaminobutanoate:pyruvate aminotransferase reaction (EC 2.6.1.76), part of ectoine biosynthesis. L-2,4-diaminobutyrate (C4H10N2O2) donates its gamma-amino group to pyruvate (C3H4O3), yielding L-alanine (C3H7NO2) and L-aspartate-4-semialdehyde (C4H7NO3). Atom balance: left C7H14N2O5, right C7H14N2O5 - balanced. The enzyme (EctB) typically operates in the direction of DABA production from aspartate semialdehyde in vivo, but as written this represents the reverse; transamination reactions are inherently reversible though physiologically driven toward DABA for ectoine synthesis.

rxn04002.other_comments: This is the second oxidation step in the sterol C4-demethylation pathway, catalyzed by the sterol-4alpha-methyl oxidase (SMO/ERG25-type, EC 1.14.18.9). It oxidizes the 4-hydroxymethyl group to the 4-carbaldehyde using NADPH and O2, producing 2 water molecules. Stoichiometry is balanced: a hydroxymethyl (CH2OH) is oxidized to an aldehyde (CHO), consuming one O2 and one NADPH+H+, yielding 2 H2O and NADP+. Atoms (C, H, O, N) and charges balance correctly.

rxn03546.other_comments: This reaction describes the NADP+-dependent oxidation of 6-hydroxyhexanoate to 6-oxohexanoate (adipate semialdehyde), catalyzed by an oxidoreductase (e.g., EC 1.1.1.258). The stoichiometry is balanced: the primary alcohol (6-hydroxyhexanoate) is oxidized to an aldehyde (6-oxohexanoate) with concomitant reduction of NADP+ to NADPH plus release of one proton. Atoms and charges balance correctly with the H+ included.

rxn00340.other_comments: This is asparagine synthetase (ammonia-dependent), AspA/AsnA reaction (EC 6.3.1.1). It uses ATP to ligate ammonia to L-aspartate, forming L-asparagine, AMP, and PPi. Atom and charge balance check: reactants ATP + NH3 + Asp; products PPi + AMP + 2 H+ + Asn. The reaction is balanced, with PPi release and 2 protons accounting for the ATP-to-AMP cleavage. In vivo, PPi hydrolysis drives the reaction strongly toward asparagine synthesis, so it is effectively irreversible in the forward direction.

rxn01041.other_comments: This reaction represents D-xylose dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.175), oxidizing D-xylose at C1 to D-xylono-1,5-lactone (or 1,4-lactone) using NAD+ as the electron acceptor, producing NADH and H+. Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and charge balance correctly.

rxn03033.other_comments: This is an NADP+-dependent oxidoreductase reaction where the secondary alcohol (3-hydroxy group) of benzyl (2R,3S)-2-methyl-3-hydroxybutanoate is oxidized to a ketone (benzyl 2-methyl-3-oxobutanoate), with reduction of NADP+ to NADPH and release of a proton. Stoichiometry is balanced: the oxidation removes 2 H (one as hydride to form NADPH, one as H+), consistent with alcohol-to-ketone conversion. Charge and atom balance are correct.

rxn01894.other_comments: This is the 4-oxalocrotonate decarboxylase reaction (EC 4.1.1.77) in the meta-cleavage pathway for aromatic compound degradation. 4-Oxalocrotonate (2-oxohex-3-enedioate / 2-hydroxymuconate tautomer derivative) is decarboxylated to 2-oxopent-4-enoate (2-keto-4-pentenoate) plus CO2, with a proton consumed. Decarboxylations releasing CO2 are essentially irreversible under physiological conditions, driving the catabolic pathway forward.

rxn00378.other_comments: This is sulfite dehydrogenase (sulfite:ferricytochrome-c oxidoreductase, EC 1.8.2.1). Checking the balance: Sulfite (SO3^2-) + H2O -> Sulfate (SO4^2-) gains one O from water; H2O provides 2 H, released as 2 H+. The overall charge: left side SO3^2- (-2) + 2 Cyt c3+ (+6, relative) = +4; right side SO4^2- (-2) + 3 H+ (+3) + 2 Cyt c2+ (+4) = +5. Mass: O balances (3+1=4); H: 2 from water on left vs 3 H+ on right. rxn00855.other_comments: This reaction is putrescine acetyltransferase (spermidine/spermine N1-acetyltransferase family), transferring an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to putrescine, yielding N-acetylputrescine and CoA. Acetyl-CoA-dependent acetyltransferases are strongly thermodynamically favorable in the forward direction due to the high-energy thioester bond.

The thioester cleavage of acetyl-CoA is highly exergonic, so the reaction proceeds in the acetylation direction in vivo.

rxn01244.other_comments: This is the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase (E1 component, EC 1.2.4.4) reaction for valine catabolism. 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate (the keto acid of valine) undergoes oxidative decarboxylation, releasing CO2 and transferring the 2-methylpropanoyl (isobutyryl) group to the lipoyl moiety, forming S-(2-methylpropionyl)-dihydrolipoamide. Note that the formal acceptor should be the oxidized lipoamide (lipoyllysine), and the product is the acylated dihydrolipoamide; the H+ and atom balance is consistent. The reaction is strongly driven forward by the irreversible loss of CO2.

rxn02154.other_comments: This is the hydrolysis of deamido-NAD (nicotinate adenine dinucleotide, NaAD) at the pyrophosphate bond, yielding AMP and nicotinate ribonucleotide (nicotinate mononucleotide, NaMN). rxn06200.other_comments: This is the PEP-dependent phosphorylation of Enzyme I (EI) in the bacterial phosphotransferase system (PTS). PEP transfers its phosphoryl group to a histidine residue (N-pros/N-pi nitrogen) of the protein, producing pyruvate and phosphohistidine. The reaction is balanced: phosphate transferred from PEP to His, with pyruvate as the dephospho product.

rxn02490.other_comments: This is the reaction catalyzed by inositol-tetrakisphosphate 1-kinase (ITPK1, EC 2.7.1.159), transferring the gamma-phosphate of ATP to the 1-position of Ins(3,4,5,6)P4 to form Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5. Stoichiometry is balanced: ATP + Ins(3,4,5,6)P4 yields ADP + H+ + Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5. Mass and charge balance hold with the released proton. ITPK1 is known to be a bifunctional, reversible enzyme that can act as both a kinase and a phosphatase, so the in vivo direction depends on cellular ATP/ADP ratios and substrate concentrations.

rxn06614.other_comments: This is protein-L-isoaspartate O-methyltransferase (PIMT, EC 2.1.1.77), a protein repair enzyme. SAM donates a methyl group to the alpha-carboxyl of an L-isoaspartyl residue, producing the methyl ester and SAH. Stoichiometry is balanced (one methyl transferred). In vivo the reaction proceeds in the methylation direction as the first step of isoaspartate repair; the methyl ester is unstable and spontaneously converts to a succinimide intermediate, pulling the reaction forward.

rxn03132.other_comments: This is a fucosyltransferase (Lewis blood group, FUT3-type alpha-1,4-fucosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.65) reaction. GDP-L-fucose donates an L-fucose residue to the GlcNAc of a type 1 chain (Gal-beta-1,3-GlcNAc-R), forming an alpha-1,4 linkage and releasing GDP. The stoichiometry is balanced: one fucosyl group is transferred, GDP-fucose becomes GDP, and the acceptor gains the fucose. Glycosyltransferase reactions using sugar nucleotide donors are strongly exergonic (hydrolysis of the glycosidic-phosphate bond) and proceed essentially irreversibly in the forward direction in vivo.

rxn02447.other_comments: This reaction represents the 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (17beta-HSD) interconversion of androst-5-ene-3beta,17beta-diol (androstenediol) and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHA/DHEA), coupled to NADP+/NADPH. The 17-hydroxyl of androstenediol is oxidized to the 17-keto group of DHEA, with reduction of NADP+ to NADPH + H+. Stoichiometry is balanced: one hydride and one proton are transferred to the cofactor. The reaction is catalyzed by NADP-dependent 17beta-HSD isoforms and is generally reversible, though in vivo flux often favors reduction of DHEA to androstenediol (i.e., the reverse direction) depending on isoform and cofactor ratios.

rxn05127.other_comments: This is the NADP-dependent oxidation of gamma-glutamyl-gamma-aminobutyraldehyde to gamma-glutamyl-GABA (gamma-glutamyl-4-aminobutyrate), catalyzed by an aldehyde dehydrogenase (e.g., PuuC in the putrescine utilization pathway). The aldehyde is oxidized to a carboxylic acid, consuming water and NADP+ and producing NADPH plus 2 protons. The atom and charge balance are consistent: oxidation of an aldehyde to a carboxylate adds one oxygen (from H2O) and releases two electrons (to NADP+) and two protons. Stoichiometry is correct.

errors: Stoichiometric/atom imbalance: the substrate 5beta-Pregnane-11beta,21-diol-3,20-dione (a saturated 5beta-pregnane) has two more hydrogen atoms than corticosterone (which contains a 4,5-double bond), so converting substrate to product requires removal of 2 H (oxidation), consistent with NADP+ -> NADPH + H+; however the equation as written uses NADP (not NADP+) which is ambiguous, and the direction implies introduction of the delta-4 double bond
rxn14379.other_comments: This reaction is the 5beta-reductase reaction (named as a 4,5-oxidoreductase). The named enzyme reduces the delta-4 double bond of corticosterone using NADPH to give the 5beta-dihydro product (11beta,21-dihydroxy-5beta-pregnane-3,20-dione). In vivo, steroid 5beta-reductase (AKR1D1) catalyzes the reductive direction (corticosterone + NADPH -> 5beta-dihydro product + NADP+), which is the reverse of the equation as written. The forward direction as written would be oxidative reintroduction of the 4,5 double bond, which is not the physiological reaction.

rxn04896.other_comments: This reaction describes glutathione S-transferase-mediated conjugation of glutathione (GSH) with chloroacetyl chloride, an acyl halide. The thiol of GSH attacks the carbonyl carbon, displacing one chloride to form the thioester S-(2-chloroacetyl)glutathione and releasing chloride ion (Cl-). The mass and charge balance check out: chloroacetyl chloride (ClCH2COCl) has two chlorines; one remains on the alpha carbon of the chloroacetyl group bound to GSH, and one is released as Cl-. The reaction is effectively irreversible in vivo because acyl halides are highly electrophilic and reactive, and chloride release makes the conjugation thermodynamically favorable and unidirectional.

rxn12095.other_comments: This is an O-methyltransferase reaction in colchicine biosynthesis. SAM donates a methyl group to isoandrocymbine, producing S-adenosyl-homocysteine (SAH) and O-methylandrocymbine. The methyl transfer to an oxygen (or hydroxyl) releases a proton, which is consistent with the stoichiometry shown. Atom and charge balance appear correct: one methyl group is transferred from SAM to the substrate, SAM becomes SAH, and a H+ is released. SAM-dependent methyltransferase reactions are generally thermodynamically favorable and effectively irreversible in vivo, proceeding in the direction of methylation.

rxn12587.other_comments: This appears to be a membrane transport reaction (TRANS-RXN) for D-Mannitol, likely a proton-coupled symporter or facilitated transporter. rxn03913.other_comments: This reaction represents the Delta24(28) sterol reductase step (ERG4) in ergosterol biosynthesis, written in reverse. The biological flux runs in the reverse direction (ergostatetraenol + NADPH + H+ -> ergosterol + NADP+). Stoichiometry is balanced for atoms and charge.

rxn00220.other_comments: This is the glucose-6-phosphatase reaction, hydrolyzing glucose-6-phosphate to free glucose and inorganic phosphate. The reaction is balanced: H2O + glucose-6-phosphate (C6H11O9P) yields glucose (C6H12O6) + phosphate (HPO4/Pi). Atoms and charges balance correctly. Physiologically this hydrolysis of a phosphate ester is highly exergonic and runs in the direction of glucose formation, important in gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis in liver/kidney.

rxn11764.other_comments: This is the thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) reaction, transferring a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the sulfur of 6-mercaptopurine to form 6-methylmercaptopurine and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. rxn01798.other_comments: This is a malonyl-CoA dependent N-malonyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.114) transferring the malonyl group from malonyl-CoA onto the amino nitrogen of D-tryptophan, producing N-malonyl-D-tryptophan and releasing CoA. rxn04854.other_comments: This represents a cytochrome P450 (CYP epoxygenase, e.g. CYP2C/2J) catalyzed epoxidation of arachidonate (C20H32O2) at the 14,15 double bond to form 14,15-epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (14,15-EET). rxn04209.other_comments: This is a gibberellin 3-beta-hydroxylase (GA3ox) reaction, a 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase. GA9 is hydroxylated to GA4. rxn01619.other_comments: This is the aldol cleavage of 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-L-rhamnonate (a 6-carbon 2-keto-3-deoxy sugar acid, C6H9O5-) by 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-L-rhamnonate aldolase, yielding pyruvate (C3, 3 carbons) and L-lactaldehyde (C3, 3 carbons). rxn04089.other_comments: This represents the biosynthetic coupling of the monoterpene indole alkaloids vindoline and catharanthine into the dimeric alkaloid 3',4'-anhydrovinblastine, catalyzed by a peroxidase in Catharanthus roseus. In vivo this proceeds in the direction of dimer formation.

rxn01391.other_comments: This is an NAD+-dependent polyol (pentitol) dehydrogenase oxidizing a sugar alcohol to a ketose, releasing NADH and H+. rxn05539.other_comments: This is an ABC-type oligopeptide import transporter that uses ATP hydrolysis to drive movement of the dipeptide Cys-Gly across a membrane. rxn08045.other_comments: This is the WecG/RffM (or related) reaction in enterobacterial common antigen (ECA) biosynthesis. UDP-N-acetyl-D-mannosaminuronate (UDP-ManNAcA) transfers its ManNAcA moiety onto undecaprenyl-diphospho-N-acetylglucosamine (Lipid I, GlcNAc-PP-Und), forming undecaprenyl-diphospho-GlcNAc-ManNAcA (Lipid II) and releasing UDP. rxn03981.other_comments: This reaction represents mycothione reductase running in reverse (the named oxidoreductase): two reduced mycothiol (MSH) molecules are oxidized to form one mycothione (MSSM, the disulfide), with NAD+ reduced to NADH and a proton released. rxn01399.other_comments: This reaction is the UDP-glucose:pyridoxine 5'-O-beta-D-glucosyltransferase (EC 2.4.1.160). It transfers a glucosyl moiety from UDP-glucose to the 5'-hydroxyl of pyridoxine (pyridoxol), producing 5'-O-beta-D-glucosylpyridoxine and releasing UDP. Stoichiometry is balanced: the glucose unit is transferred from UDP-glucose to pyridoxine, with UDP as the leaving group. Glycosyltransferase reactions using sugar nucleotide donors are thermodynamically favorable in the direction of glycoside formation due to cleavage of the UDP-sugar bond.

rxn02505.other_comments: This reaction is the oxidation of an aldehyde (3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestan-26-al) to the corresponding carboxylic acid (3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoate/cholestanate) using NAD+ as the electron acceptor, with water as a co-substrate. This is a step in bile acid biosynthesis (the conversion toward THCA/trihydroxycoprostanic acid). The stoichiometry is balanced: aldehyde + H2O is oxidized to the carboxylic acid, releasing 2 H+ and reducing NAD+ to NADH (the aldehyde carbon goes from oxidation state +1 to +3, a 2-electron oxidation matching one NADH). Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and charge balance check out.

rxn04040.other_comments: This reaction represents the inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 6-kinase (IP3 6-kinase) activity, which phosphorylates Ins(1,4,5)P3 to Ins(1,4,5,6)P4 using ATP. The stoichiometry is balanced: ATP donates a phosphate to the 6-position of the inositol ring, yielding ADP, a proton, and the tetrakisphosphate product. Mass and charge are balanced (the H+ accounts for the proton released upon phosphoryl transfer). Kinase reactions of this type are strongly exergonic due to ATP hydrolysis coupling and proceed in the phosphorylation (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn06653.other_comments: This reaction represents UDP-galactose:ceramide galactosyltransferase (CGT, EC 2.4.1.45) acting on a hydroxy-fatty-acyl ceramide. UDP-galactose donates galactose to the 1-hydroxyl of the 2-(2-hydroxyacyl)sphingosine (a hydroxy ceramide), yielding galactosylceramide and UDP. Oxidoreductases of this type (3-oxoester/hydroxyester reductases) are typically reversible, though in vivo they often favor ketone reduction (NADPH consumption).

errors: The substrate is generically named '(R)-3-Hydroxyacyl-[acyl-carrier protein]' but the reaction is annotated as specific for the n-C4:0 chain; it should be (R)-3-hydroxybutanoyl-[ACP] for consistency with the product but-2-enoyl-[ACP]

Mechanistic stereochemistry note: bacterial FabA/FabZ dehydratases typically act on (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-ACP to give trans-2-enoyl-ACP, so the (R) designation is acceptable, but the generic vs specific naming mismatch is the main issue
rxn07981.other_comments: This is a 3-hydroxyacyl-ACP dehydratase (FabA/FabZ type) step in fatty acid biosynthesis (FAS II), removing water from (R)-3-hydroxybutanoyl-ACP to form trans-but-2-enoyl-ACP (crotonyl-ACP). Stoichiometry is balanced (loss of one H2O). Although the dehydration step itself can be reversible in vitro, in vivo it proceeds toward the enoyl product as part of the chain-elongation cycle.

rxn05049.other_comments: This reaction describes the hydrolysis of choloyl-CoA (cholyl-CoA) thioester by a thioesterase/hydrolase, yielding free cholate (cholic acid anion) and coenzyme A, with release of a proton. The stoichiometry is balanced: water provides the OH to the carboxylate and H to CoA-SH, and one proton is released to account for the ionization state of the carboxylate product. Thioester hydrolysis is thermodynamically favorable (highly exergonic) and effectively irreversible in vivo, proceeding in the direction of cholate + CoA formation.

errors: Ribonucleotide reductase acts on the diphosphate (or in some organisms the triphosphate) level, but the proper substrate for class I/II RNR is GDP, not GTP; if this is a class III (anaerobic) or specific NTP reductase, GTP can be a substrate, so the level may be acceptable depending on enzyme class

The reaction as written is not balanced: reduction of the 2'-OH to 2'-H removes one oxygen atom. GTP (C10H12N5O14P3 charge form) to dGTP loses one O. With trdrd (dithiol) -> trdox (disulfide) supplying 2 H (2 electrons + 2 protons) and consuming the extra H+, the products should include H2O. Check: GTP + 2[H] -> dGTP + H2O. The dithiol provides 2 H. Written as trdrd + H+ giving trdox + H2O + dGTP from GTP - this accounts for removal of O as water and the 2 H from thioredoxin, leaving net consumption of the extra H+ to balance charge. Approximately balanced, but verify proton count carefully.
rxn05234.other_comments: This represents ribonucleotide reductase-type chemistry: reduction of the ribose 2'-OH of GTP to give 2'-deoxyGTP (dGTP), using reduced thioredoxin (dithiol) as electron donor, which becomes oxidized thioredoxin (disulfide), releasing water. In vivo this is strongly driven toward dNTP synthesis (forward) due to thioredoxin regeneration by thioredoxin reductase/NADPH.

rxn09439.other_comments: This represents one elongation cycle of mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS), extending decanoyl-ACP (C10) to dodecanoyl-ACP (C12). The condensation of malonyl-ACP with the acyl-ACP releases CO2 and free ACP, then two NADPH-dependent reductions (with intermediate dehydration releasing H2O) yield the saturated C12 product. Carbon balance: C10 acyl + C3 malonyl - CO2 = C12, which checks out. Redox and proton balance are consistent with two reduction steps.

rxn01430.other_comments: This is an acyltransferase reaction transferring the caffeoyl group from caffeoyl-CoA to a hydroxyl group of isocitrate, releasing free CoA and forming caffeoylisocitrate. The atom balance is consistent: caffeoyl-CoA donates the acyl group (loss of CoA-SH), and isocitrate accepts it via ester formation, with CoA released. Stoichiometry (1:1 substrates to 1:1 products) is correct. Acyl-CoA transferases that form esters from thioester high-energy bonds are thermodynamically favorable and typically operate in the biosynthetic (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn03145.other_comments: This is the THCA-CoA ligase reaction (also known as bile acid CoA ligase, VLCS/SLC27A2 family), activating the bile acid intermediate 3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanate to its CoA thioester. The reaction is an AMP-forming (acyl-CoA synthetase type) ligase: ATP + CoA + carboxylic acid -> AMP + PPi + acyl-CoA, with release of H+. The atom and charge balance is consistent. Although written as reversible, the reaction is driven forward in vivo by subsequent hydrolysis of PPi to 2 Pi by inorganic pyrophosphatase, making it effectively irreversible toward CoA-thioester formation.

errors: The substrate 'Isoleucine' and product 'L-Isoleucine' appear to be the same compound or the distinction is ambiguous; a permease (transport reaction) should show the same metabolite on both sides distinguished by compartment, not a chemical transformation
No compartment designations are provided (e.g., extracellular vs cytoplasmic), which are essential for a transport reaction
If interpreted as a chemical interconversion, there is no enzymatic basis for converting generic 'Isoleucine' to 'L-Isoleucine'
rxn11110.other_comments: This is annotated as a branched chain amino acid permease, implying a proton-coupled symport transport of isoleucine across a membrane. As written, both sides carry one H+ and one isoleucine species, so it is mass/charge balanced, but the lack of compartment labels makes the transport meaningless as stated. Proton symporters are typically driven by the proton motive force, often functioning to import the substrate.

rxn01925.other_comments: This is the dihydrolipoamide S-acyltransferase (E2) component reaction of the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex. Isobutyryl-CoA (2-methylpropanoyl-CoA) transfers its acyl group to the dihydrolipoamide thiol, yielding free CoA and S-(2-methylpropanoyl)-dihydrolipoamide. Stoichiometry is balanced: the 2-methylpropanoyl group is transferred from the CoA thioester to the dihydrolipoamide sulfhydryl. In vivo this proceeds in the catabolic (forward) direction toward CoA release as part of branched-chain amino acid (valine) degradation.

rxn03325.other_comments: This is the isopenicillin N acyltransferase (IAT/acyl-CoA:isopenicillin N acyltransferase) reaction. It exchanges the L-2-aminoadipoyl side chain of isopenicillin N for a phenylacetyl group from phenylacetyl-CoA, producing penicillin G (benzylpenicillin), free CoA, and L-2-aminoadipate. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: water hydrolyzes the amide, releasing L-2-aminoadipate and a proton, while the phenylacetyl group is transferred from CoA to the 6-aminopenicillanic acid moiety. Stoichiometry appears correct.

rxn14295.other_comments: This reaction represents a 3,4-isomerase converting dTDP-4-oxo-2,6-dideoxy-L-mannose (a 4-keto sugar) to dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-L-erythro-hexos-3-ulose (a 3-keto sugar). Both substrate and product are isomers with the same molecular formula (the carbonyl group migrates from C4 to C3), so the reaction is stoichiometrically balanced with a 1:1 ratio. Isomerases of this type are typically near-equilibrium and reversible, with directionality in vivo driven by subsequent biosynthetic steps in deoxysugar pathways.

rxn03416.other_comments: This reaction represents the isomerization between Retinene 2 (all-trans-3,4-didehydroretinal, also called all-trans-retinal 2) and its 11-cis isomer (11-cis-3,4-didehydroretinal / 11-cis-dehydroretinal). It is a 1:1 cis-trans isomerization, so the stoichiometry is balanced with identical molecular formulas (C20H26O) on both sides. Such retinoid isomerizations are part of the visual cycle (porphyropsin system) and are catalyzed by retinal isomerases; the equilibrium can be driven in either direction depending on enzyme and light conditions.

rxn04288.other_comments: This is a PLP-dependent transaminase reaction transferring an amino group from L-glutamate to dTDP-3-oxo-4,6-dideoxy-D-glucose, yielding 2-oxoglutarate and the aminated sugar dTDP-3-amino-3,4,6-trideoxy-D-glucose. The substrate naming is consistent: the 3-oxo (keto) group at C3 is converted to a 3-amino group, and the 4,6-dideoxy/3,4,6-trideoxy nomenclature reflects the additional deoxygenation at C3 upon amination. Stoichiometry is balanced (one amino group transferred, one keto group generated). Transaminases are generally reversible in vitro; however, in vivo this step in deoxysugar biosynthesis is typically driven in the aminating (forward, biosynthetic) direction toward the 3-amino sugar.

rxn13661.other_comments: This is the final methylation step in menaquinone biosynthesis catalyzed by MenG/UbiE, transferring a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to 2-demethylmenaquinone-7 (2dmmq7) to form menaquinone-7 (MK-7), releasing S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) and a proton. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: the methyl group transferred from SAM accounts for the added carbon/hydrogens on the menaquinone product, and the H+ balances the charge. SAM-dependent methyltransferase reactions are thermodynamically favorable and physiologically driven in the forward (biosynthetic) direction.

rxn05374.other_comments: This is an enoyl-ACP reductase step in branched-chain (iso/anteiso) fatty acid biosynthesis. NADPH reduces the trans-2 double bond of 10-methyl-trans-dodec-2-enoyl-ACP to yield the saturated 10-methyl-dodecanoyl-ACP. Stoichiometry is balanced: one NADPH + H+ provides the two electrons and proton needed to reduce the alkene, regenerating NADP+. The product correctly loses the 2-enoyl double bond. In vivo, enoyl reductases drive fatty acid synthesis in the reductive (forward) direction.

errors: Mass/atom imbalance: the condensation of malonyl-ACP (3 carbons in acyl portion) with 6-methyl-heptanoyl-ACP (8 carbons) with loss of CO2 should yield a 10-carbon 3-oxoacyl chain (8-methyl-3-oxo-decanoyl-ACP), not the 9-carbon 8-methyl-3-oxo-nonanoyl-ACP shown; the product carbon count is off by one

One ACP is consumed/released improperly relative to standard FAS condensation: two ACP-thioesters enter and one product-ACP plus free ACP should leave, which is balanced in count, but the product naming inconsistency indicates the chain-length error
rxn05417.other_comments: This is a beta-ketoacyl-ACP synthase (KAS) type Claisen condensation reaction in fatty acid biosynthesis, extending a branched 6-methyl-heptanoyl primer by a two-carbon unit from malonyl-ACP with decarboxylation. Such condensations are essentially irreversible in vivo due to CO2 release.

rxn07098.other_comments: This represents isopenicillin N acyltransferase (IAT/penDE), which hydrolytically removes the L-2-aminoadipoyl side chain of isopenicillin N (yielding 6-aminopenicillanic acid, 6-APA, plus L-2-aminoadipate) and then transfers an acyl group from an acyl-CoA (e.g., phenylacetyl-CoA) to 6-APA to form hydrophobic penicillins. The generic 'Penam' placeholder is too vague and the acyl transfer is not properly represented stoichiometrically.

rxn03961.other_comments: This reaction represents a 3-beta-hydroxysteroid:NADP+ 3-oxidoreductase. Lophenol (4alpha-methyl-5alpha-cholest-7-en-3beta-ol) is oxidized at the C3 hydroxyl to the corresponding 3-oxo (ketone) compound, 4alpha-methyl-5alpha-cholest-7-en-3-one, with reduction of NADP+ to NADPH. The hydroxyl-to-ketone oxidation releases one H+ along with the hydride transferred to NADP+, so the proton balance (one H+ on the product side) and electron/hydride accounting are correct. The reaction is stoichiometrically balanced as written.

rxn00579.other_comments: This is sucrose synthase (EC 2.4.1.13), which catalyzes the transfer of a glucosyl group from UDP-glucose to fructose forming sucrose and UDP. The reaction is correctly balanced: UDP-glucose (C15H24N2O17P2) + fructose (C6H12O6) gives UDP (C9H14N2O12P2) + sucrose (C12H22O11), with atoms and charges conserved.

rxn01804.other_comments: This reaction represents the dehydration of citramalyl-CoA (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-related branched intermediate; specifically 2-methylmalyl-CoA / citramalyl-CoA) to itaconyl-CoA, catalyzed by a hydro-lyase. The stoichiometry is balanced: citramalyl-CoA (C26H42N7O20P3S as the acyl-CoA) loses one H2O to form itaconyl-CoA. Hydro-lyase (dehydratase) reactions of this type are typically reversible in vivo; in the itaconate degradation pathway the physiological direction is hydration (itaconyl-CoA + H2O -> citramalyl-CoA), which is the reverse of the way written here.

errors: Hydrogen/charge imbalance: O2 + 4 substrate should account for protons and electrons. The condensation of two hydroxylamino groups to an azoxy linkage releases water, but the overall mass/H balance does not close with this stoichiometry. Two 2-hydroxylamino-4,6-dinitrotoluene (C7H7N3O5) molecules condense to one azoxytoluene (C14H10N6O9) + H2O, so 4 substrate yield 2 azoxy products + 2 H2O, not 4 H2O. rxn11692.other_comments: This reaction represents oxidative dimerization (condensation) of two hydroxylamino-dinitrotoluene molecules to form an azoxy-linked dimer (a known TNT/aminonitrotoluene transformation product), with O2 acting as the oxidant. The conceptual chemistry is plausible, but the written stoichiometry appears unbalanced in H and O.

rxn01157.other_comments: This reaction describes the intramolecular cyclization of D-glutamate to form 5-oxo-D-proline (D-pyroglutamate) with release of water, the D-enantiomer analog of pyroglutamate formation. The stoichiometry is balanced: D-glutamate (C5H9NO4) loses one water (H2O) to form 5-oxo-D-proline (C5H7NO3). Atoms balance: C5=C5, H9=H7+H2, N1=N1, O4=O3+O1. The lyase reaction is thermodynamically favorable in the cyclizing/lactam-forming direction in vivo, though such cyclizations can be slowly reversible.

rxn07989.other_comments: This is the 3-oxoacyl-ACP reductase (FabG) reaction in fatty acid biosynthesis, reducing a beta-keto group to a beta-hydroxyl using NADPH. The carbon count (C14:1, cis-7) and ACP carrier are preserved. Stoichiometry balances: one NADPH + H+ reduces the ketone to hydroxyl, yielding NADP+. The reaction is written reduction direction.

rxn01844.other_comments: This is the sphingomyelinase (sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase, EC 3.1.4.12) reaction. Sphingomyelin is hydrolyzed by water to yield ceramide and phosphocholine, with release of a proton. Stoichiometry is balanced: the phosphodiester bond between ceramide and phosphocholine is cleaved hydrolytically. As a hydrolase reaction in vivo, it proceeds in the catabolic (forward) direction toward ceramide and phosphocholine.

rxn07869.other_comments: This is a hydrolysis reaction where cis-zeatin riboside (a cytokinin ribonucleoside) is cleaved by water to release D-ribose and cis-zeatin (the free base cytokinin). The reaction is stoichiometrically balanced: cis-zeatin riboside consists of the cis-zeatin base linked to ribose via an N-glycosidic bond; hydrolysis adds water across this bond yielding free ribose and the free base. Atom and charge balance check out. Such purine/cytokinin nucleoside hydrolase reactions are thermodynamically favorable and proceed in the hydrolytic (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn04447.other_comments: This is the NAD-dependent oxidation of UDP-glucose at the C4 position (UDP-glucose 4,6-dehydratase / related epimerase-type chemistry) producing UDP-3-ketoglucose (more precisely a UDP-4-keto sugar intermediate in many pathways; here written as UDP-3-ketoglucose). The reaction transfers a hydride to NAD forming NADH + H+. Stoichiometry is balanced: one NAD oxidizes one sugar hydroxyl to a keto group with release of NADH and a proton. The atoms and charges balance correctly.

Charge and oxygen balance are off by one water molecule as written.
rxn03216.other_comments: This represents the spontaneous/enzymatic intramolecular cyclization step in benzophenanthridine alkaloid (sanguinarine) biosynthesis, where 6-hydroxyprotopine undergoes ring closure with loss of water to form dihydrosanguinarine. The reaction proceeds in the direction of dihydrosanguinarine formation in vivo.

rxn02531.other_comments: This is a UDP-glucose dependent glucosyltransferase reaction transferring a glucosyl moiety from UDP-glucose to the 7-OH of daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin) to form daphnin, releasing UDP. Glycosyltransferase reactions of this type are thermodynamically favorable and biosynthetic in vivo.

rxn07848.other_comments: This is the F420-independent (here NADP-dependent) methylene-H4MPT dehydrogenase reaction interconverting 5,10-methylenetetrahydromethanopterin and 5,10-methenyltetrahydromethanopterin in methanogens/methylotrophs. The enzyme (e.g., MtdA/Hmd-type NADP-dependent methylenetetrahydromethanopterin dehydrogenase) operates reversibly depending on the redox poise and direction of the C1 pathway (methanogenesis vs CO2 fixation/formaldehyde oxidation).

rxn07861.other_comments: This reaction represents the hydrolysis of isopentenyladenosine (a cytokinin nucleoside) into the free base N6-(dimethylallyl)adenine plus the sugar. The substrate is the riboside (adenine + ribose linked); cleavage of the N-glycosidic bond by water yields D-ribose and the free purine base. Atom balance: isopentenyladenosine (C15H21N5O4) + H2O (H2O) gives D-ribose (C5H10O5) + N6-dimethylallyladenine (C10H13N5), which balances correctly (C15H23N5O5 on each side). The 'dimethylallyl' naming is loose but corresponds to the isopentenyl/prenyl substituent. Hydrolytic N-glycosidase/purine nucleosidase reactions are essentially irreversible toward hydrolysis in vivo.

rxn08772.other_comments: This is the ArnT-catalyzed transfer of 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (Ara4N) from the lipid carrier undecaprenyl phosphate-Ara4N onto lipid A of LPS at the periplasmic face, modifying lipid A (a polymyxin/cationic peptide resistance mechanism). The glycosyl transfer is essentially irreversible/forward in vivo, regenerating undecaprenyl phosphate. The H+ stoichiometry should be checked/balanced; charge and element balance for the sugar transfer itself is plausible but the 2.0 H+ term is suspect.

rxn03106.other_comments: This is the oxidation of an aldehyde (3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy-5beta-cholestan-26-al) to a carboxylic acid (3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy-5beta-cholestanate), a step in bile acid biosynthesis. The reaction consumes H2O and NAD+ and produces NADH, 2 H+, and the carboxylate. Mass and charge balance: aldehyde (RCHO) + H2O -> RCOOH + 2H + 2e; the 2 electrons reduce NAD+ to NADH, releasing one H+ from substrate oxidation plus accounting gives 2 H+ overall, which balances correctly.

rxn04135.other_comments: This is a cytochrome P450-type monooxygenase reaction (limonene 6-hydroxylase / 6-monooxygenase). It hydroxylates (+)-limonene at C6 to form (+)-trans-carveol, consuming NADPH, O2, and H+, producing NADP+ and H2O. The stoichiometry is balanced: one oxygen atom from O2 is incorporated into the substrate (forming the hydroxyl), and the other is reduced to water using electrons from NADPH. Atom and charge balance check out.

rxn08518.other_comments: This is the formate hydrogenlyase (FHL) reaction, which decomposes formic acid (HCOOH) into CO2 and H2. Written as Formate + H+ <=> CO2 + H2, the reaction is stoichiometrically balanced: C (1=1), O (2=2), H (formate HCOO- has 1 H + 1 H+ = 2 H total, matching H2's 2 H), and charge (-1 + 1 = 0, balanced). In vivo (e.g., in E. coli under anaerobic fermentation), the FHL complex (FdhH + Hyd-3) catalyzes this reaction essentially irreversibly in the forward direction to dispose of excess formate and acidify-buffer the cytoplasm, producing H2 gas.

rxn04626.other_comments: This is a glycosyltransferase reaction (EC 2.4.2.-) transferring a xylose moiety from UDP-xylose to rutin (quercetin 3-O-rutinoside), forming quercetin 3-(2G-xylosylrutinoside) and releasing UDP. The xylosyl group is added to the 2'' position of the glucose in rutin. Stoichiometry is balanced: the xylose unit (C5H8O4) is transferred from UDP-xylose to the acceptor, with UDP released. Glycosyltransferase reactions using UDP-sugar donors are strongly thermodynamically favored toward transfer in vivo.

rxn01550.other_comments: This is the diamine oxidase (copper-containing amine oxidase) reaction. Histamine is oxidatively deaminated using O2 and H2O to yield imidazole-4-acetaldehyde, ammonia, and hydrogen peroxide. The reaction is balanced: histamine (C5H9N3) + O2 + H2O gives imidazoleacetaldehyde (C5H6N2O) + NH3 + H2O2. rxn10583.other_comments: This reaction describes the hydrolysis of dATP to dADP, releasing inorganic phosphate. The reaction is balanced: dATP (C10H12N5O12P3 with appropriate protonation) + H2O yields dADP + Pi + H+. Mass and charge are conserved when accounting for the released proton. This is a nucleoside triphosphate phosphohydrolase activity (gamma-phosphate cleavage).

rxn05416.other_comments: This is an enoyl-ACP reductase step in fatty acid/branched-chain acyl-ACP biosynthesis. NADPH and H+ reduce the trans-2 double bond of 6-methyl-trans-hept-2-enoyl-ACP to give the saturated 6-methyl-heptanoyl-ACP, regenerating NADP+. Atoms and charges balance (the enoyl C=C is reduced by addition of 2 H from NADPH + H+). In vivo the enoyl reductase step in the elongation cycle is essentially irreversible toward reduction.

rxn08133.other_comments: This is an aminopeptidase hydrolyzing the dipeptide L-prolylglycine (Pro-Gly) into free L-proline and glycine using water. Peptide bond hydrolysis is thermodynamically favorable and physiologically irreversible in vivo, so the forward (hydrolytic) direction is correct.

errors: The reaction as written shows identical species on both sides with no compartment distinction, making it appear as a null/identity reaction. Proton symport stoichiometry typically couples 1 H+ per substrate; using 2.0 H+ may be incorrect depending on the charge balance. N-Acetyl-L-glutamate carries a net negative charge (-2 at physiological pH), so the H+:substrate ratio should be checked for charge balance.
rxn12612.other_comments: This is intended to be a proton-coupled symport transport reaction for N-Acetyl-L-glutamate. As written, both sides are identical with no compartment labels, so it represents no net change. Transport directionality depends on the proton motive force and substrate gradients, which cannot be determined without compartment annotations.

rxn00537.other_comments: This is phosphonatase (EC 3.11.1.1), which hydrolyzes the C-P bond of 2-phosphonoacetaldehyde to yield acetaldehyde and inorganic phosphate. The reaction is balanced: phosphonoacetaldehyde (C2H4O4P-, or with protonation states) plus water yields acetaldehyde (C2H4O) and phosphate plus a proton. Atom and charge balance are consistent. The enzyme proceeds via a Schiff-base intermediate and aspartyl-phosphate.

rxn07567.other_comments: This reaction represents glucosyltransfer from UDP-glucose to the isoflavonoid-derived pterocarpan (-)-maackiain, forming trifolirhizin (maackiain 3-O-glucoside) and releasing UDP. The stoichiometry is balanced: the glucosyl group is transferred from UDP-glucose to maackiain, with UDP as the leaving group. Note that the enzyme name says '7-O' but maackiain glucosylation occurs at the 3-O position; the substrate/product pairing is chemically consistent as a glucosyl transfer regardless. rxn13958.other_comments: This is the disproportionation reaction catalyzed by raffinose:raffinose 3F-alpha-D-galactosyltransferase (EC 2.4.1.166). rxn04561.other_comments: This reaction represents the epimerization/isomerization between ecgonine and pseudoecgonine, which are diastereomers (epimers at the C-2 carboxyl-bearing position) of the tropane alkaloid ecgonine. rxn02184.other_comments: This is a hydrolysis reaction (retinyl ester hydrolase / REH activity) cleaving the ester bond of 11-cis-retinyl palmitate to yield 11-cis-retinol and palmitate. Mass and charge balance: H2O adds across the ester bond; the carboxylate of palmitate is released with a proton, so the H+ on the product side balances the deprotonated palmitate (palmitate written as the anion). Atoms balance correctly. Hydrolysis of esters in aqueous cellular environments is thermodynamically favorable and proceeds in the hydrolytic (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn01638.other_comments: This reaction represents the hydrolytic ring-opening of L-5-carboxymethylhydantoin (the cyclic form) to N-carbamoyl-L-aspartate (ureidosuccinate). This is part of pyrimidine/dihydrouracil-related catabolism where hydantoin-type rings are hydrolyzed by amidohydrolases.

rxn02817.other_comments: This reaction depicts 2-oxoarginine (5-guanidino-2-oxopentanoate) undergoing decarboxylation to yield 4-guanidinobutanal (4-guanidinobutyraldehyde) and CO2. rxn14102.other_comments: This is a malate-synthase-type (R-citramalate/2-isopropylmalate synthase family) condensation: acetyl-CoA + a 2-oxo acid + water yields the corresponding substituted malate (2-alkylmalate) plus CoA and H+. rxn01371.other_comments: This is the creatine kinase reaction (EC 2.7.3.2). ATP transfers a phosphoryl group to creatine, forming phosphocreatine and ADP, with release of a proton. In vivo this reaction is highly reversible and functions as a temporal/spatial ATP buffer: it runs toward phosphocreatine synthesis when ATP is abundant (e.g., resting muscle) and toward ATP regeneration during high energy demand.
