rxn09021.other_comments: This represents the O-antigen ligase (WaaL) reaction in LPS biosynthesis, where the O16 antigen polymer (here 4 repeat units) carried on undecaprenyl (bactoprenyl) diphosphate is transferred to the core oligosaccharide-lipid A acceptor, releasing free undecaprenyl (bactoprenyl) diphosphate. The stoichiometry is balanced: the O16 antigen tetramer is transferred from the lipid carrier to the core-lipid A, and undecaprenyl diphosphate (= bactoprenyl diphosphate) is released. This ligation is physiologically driven in the forward direction toward mature LPS assembly.

rxn01164.other_comments: This reaction represents the 15-lipoxygenase (ALOX15) catalyzed dioxygenation of arachidonate. Molecular oxygen (O2) is incorporated into arachidonic acid (C20H32O2) at the C15 position to form 15(S)-hydroperoxyeicosatetraenoic acid, 15(S)-HPETE (C20H32O4). Stoichiometry is balanced: arachidonate (C20H32O2) + O2 yields 15(S)-HPETE (C20H32O4), with both carbon and oxygen atoms conserved. The reaction is essentially irreversible in vivo, proceeding in the direction of hydroperoxide formation.

rxn03196.other_comments: This describes a cytochrome P450 (likely CYP21A2-type, steroid 21-hydroxylase) monooxygenase reaction hydroxylating 17alpha-Hydroxypregnenolone at C21 to form 17alpha,21-Dihydroxypregnenolone. The stoichiometry is balanced: NADPH + O2 + H+ provide reducing equivalents and oxygen; one oxygen atom is incorporated into the substrate (new hydroxyl) and the other is reduced to water, with NADPH oxidized to NADP+. Atoms and charges balance correctly.

rxn02709.other_comments: This reaction describes the oxidation of (2S)-flavan-4-ol to (2S)-flavanone, with NADP+ reduced to NADPH. The reaction is written as oxidation (alcohol to ketone) with NADP+ as electron acceptor. Stoichiometry is balanced: the flavan-4-ol has a secondary alcohol at C4 that is oxidized to a ketone (flavanone), releasing 2 electrons and 1 proton; NADP+ accepts a hydride to form NADPH, and one H+ is released. This is consistent with EC 1.1.1.234 (flavanone 4-reductase) type chemistry. In vivo, such reductases physiologically catalyze the reduction direction (flavanone + NADPH -> flavan-4-ol), so the biological flux typically runs opposite to how this reaction is written, i.e., in the reverse direction relative to the left-to-right depiction.

rxn07644.other_comments: This is the nitrile hydratase / phenylacetamide-forming reaction. Atom balance: benzyl cyanide (phenylacetonitrile) C8H7N + H2O (H2O) = C8H9NO = 2-phenylacetamide, so it is stoichiometrically balanced. In vivo, nitrile hydratases strongly favor hydration of the nitrile to the amide (forward as written). The enzyme name 'hydro-lyase (nitrile-forming)' implies the EC convention name for the reverse reaction, but the biological flux is toward the amide.

rxn03804.other_comments: This reaction represents dihydrostreptomycin-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (streptomycin-6-phosphate reductase, EC 1.1.1.364). The aldehyde group at C6' of streptomycin 6-phosphate (the streptose moiety) is reduced to a hydroxymethyl group using NADH as the electron donor, yielding dihydrostreptomycin 6-phosphate and NAD+. The reaction is balanced: NADH + H+ donates a hydride and proton to reduce the aldehyde to an alcohol, with NAD+ released. Atoms and charges balance. In vivo, this NADH-dependent reductive step in the streptomycin biosynthetic pathway proceeds in the direction of dihydrostreptomycin 6-phosphate formation.

rxn04357.other_comments: This reaction represents a glycosyltransferase step in avermectin biosynthesis, where the sugar moiety L-oleandrose is transferred from the activated nucleotide-sugar donor (dTDP-L-oleandrose) onto the avermectin B1b aglycone acceptor, releasing dTDP and forming the avermectin B1b monosaccharide. Stoichiometry is balanced: one sugar unit is transferred and dTDP is the leaving group. Glycosyltransferase reactions using NDP-sugar donors are thermodynamically favorable and operate in the biosynthetic (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn09900.other_comments: This reaction represents an ATP-dependent L-amino acid ligase (RizA/BL00235-type) forming the dipeptide Ser-Val from L-serine and L-valine. ATP is hydrolyzed to ADP and inorganic phosphate, driving peptide bond formation. The mass and charge balance is correct: ATP (C10H12N5O13P3, -4) + Ser (C3H7NO3, 0) + Val (C5H11NO2, 0) yields ADP (-3) + Pi (HPO4, -2) + H+ (+1) + Ser-Val dipeptide (C8H16N2O4, 0). Atoms and charges balance.

rxn07812.other_comments: This is a rhamnosyltransferase reaction (EC 2.4.1.236-like) transferring an L-rhamnose moiety from UDP-L-rhamnose to the 2''-position of the glucose in hesperetin 7-O-glucoside, forming the rhamnosyl-(1->2)-glucoside (neohesperidoside) product neohesperidin, releasing UDP. The stoichiometry is balanced: one rhamnose unit (C6H10O4) is transferred from the UDP-sugar donor to the acceptor, and UDP is released. Glycosyltransferase reactions using NDP-sugar donors are thermodynamically favorable and physiologically irreversible.

rxn10497.other_comments: This is a proton symport transport reaction for dimethylamine, where both H+ and (CH3)2NH are co-transported across a membrane (typically from extracellular/periplasmic to cytoplasmic side). The reaction as written is mass and charge balanced since identical species appear on both sides, representing translocation between two compartments rather than a chemical transformation. The notation here does not show compartment labels, but the intent is symport across a membrane. Transport reactions of this nature are generally modeled as reversible unless driven by a proton motive force.

Biosynthetic aminoacyl-PG reactions proceed in the forward (synthesis) direction in vivo.

rxn00643.other_comments: This reaction represents GDP-mannose 3,5-epimerase (GME), which converts GDP-D-mannose to GDP-L-galactose. The reaction involves epimerization at the C3 and C5 positions and is stoichiometrically balanced (no atoms gained or lost, it is an intramolecular rearrangement). In vivo, this is a committed step in the ascorbate (vitamin C) biosynthesis pathway in plants (Smirnoff-Wheeler pathway), driving flux toward L-galactose and ultimately ascorbate. Although epimerases are intrinsically reversible enzymes and GME can produce both GDP-L-galactose and GDP-L-gulose, metabolic flux is directed forward in the physiological context.

rxn01823.other_comments: This is the 4-hydroxyphenylacetate/3-hydroxyphenylacetate monooxygenase (flavin-dependent hydroxylase) reaction. The substrate 3-hydroxyphenylacetate is hydroxylated at the 6-position to give homogentisate (2,5-dihydroxyphenylacetate). The stoichiometry is balanced: NADPH + O2 + H+ provides reducing equivalents and incorporates one O atom into the product while reducing the other to water. Atoms and charges balance (one O from O2 goes into the aromatic ring, the other becomes H2O; NADPH is oxidized to NADP+). As a monooxygenase consuming O2 and NADPH, it is physiologically essentially irreversible.

rxn13989.other_comments: This is a glycosyltransferase reaction (MtmGIV in the mithramycin biosynthesis pathway) transferring a D-olivose sugar from the activated nucleotide donor dTDP-D-olivose to the aglycone premithramycinone, producing premithramycin A1 and releasing dTDP. The transfer of one olivose unit and release of dTDP balances the nucleotide sugar donor; the reaction appears stoichiometrically consistent as written. Glycosyltransferases of this type strongly favor glycosyl transfer (donor cleavage), so the reaction proceeds in the biosynthetic forward direction in vivo.

rxn07432.other_comments: This reaction represents the thiamine diphosphate (TPP)-dependent decarboxylation of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate (4MOP, the alpha-keto acid of leucine, also called alpha-ketoisocaproate). The branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex (E1 component) catalyzes the decarboxylation, releasing CO2 and forming the hydroxyalkyl-TPP intermediate (3-methyl-1-hydroxybutyl-TPP). Stoichiometry is balanced: the carbon released as CO2 comes from the carboxyl group of 4MOP, and the remaining C5 acyl moiety is bound to TPP. Charges and atoms balance with the consumption of one H+.

rxn03878.other_comments: This represents the hydration of E-phenylitaconyl-CoA (2-benzylidenesuccinyl-CoA type intermediate) to form (hydroxymethylphenyl)succinyl-CoA, an enoyl-CoA hydratase-type reaction in the anaerobic degradation pathway (e.g., methylnaphthalene/phenyl-substituted itaconyl-CoA metabolism). Atoms balance: addition of one H2O (H2O + C=C double bond addition giving OH and H across the double bond). Stoichiometry of one water added to the unsaturated CoA thioester to give the hydroxylated saturated CoA thioester is consistent. The hydration step is typically driven forward in the catabolic direction in vivo, though enoyl-CoA hydratases are mechanistically reversible.

rxn10753.other_comments: This reaction describes gamma-glutamylcyclotransferase (EC 4.3.2.7 / 2.3.2.4 family) acting on 5-L-glutamyl-L-alanine, a gamma-glutamyl dipeptide. The enzyme cleaves the dipeptide, releasing free L-alanine and cyclizing the gamma-glutamyl moiety into 5-oxoproline (pyroglutamate). The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: the gamma-glutamyl-alanine substrate yields alanine plus the lactam (5-oxoproline) with intramolecular cyclization, so no extra atoms are needed.

The stoichiometry is balanced: phosphoramidate (H2N-PO3H2) donates its phosphate to glucose, leaving NH3. Atom and charge balance hold. Physiologically the reaction proceeds toward phosphate transfer and ammonia release, favored by the high group-transfer potential of the P-N bond in phosphoramidate.

However, the substrate is named 'di-O-geranyl' (C10) rather than 'di-O-geranylgeranyl' (C20), creating a carbon-count and double-bond mismatch with the diphytanyl product.

rxn07169.other_comments: This is the chloromuconate cycloisomerase reaction (involved in chloroaromatic degradation, e.g. 3-chlorocatechol pathway). 2-Chloro-cis,cis-muconate undergoes cycloisomerization with elimination of chloride to form trans-4-carboxymethylenebut-2-en-4-olide (the dienelactone, also called protoanemonin precursor/cis-dienelactone). The reaction is balanced: the substrate (C6H3ClO4 as anion) loses Cl- to form the lactone product (C6H3O4 anion). Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and charge all balance. Note the EC name given describes the reverse (lyase decyclizing) sense, but physiologically the cyclization/dechlorination proceeds in the catabolic direction shown.

rxn02824.other_comments: This reaction represents the transfer of a palmitoyl group from palmitoyl-CoA to a hydroxyl (or thiol) group on a mucus glycoprotein, releasing free CoA and forming the O-palmitoylated glycoprotein. Stoichiometry is balanced as written, with the palmitoyl moiety conserved in the transfer from the thioester (palmitoyl-CoA) to the glycoprotein acceptor. Acyltransferase reactions using acyl-CoA thioesters as acyl donors are thermodynamically favorable due to the high-energy thioester bond and proceed in the direction of acylation in vivo.

rxn07992.other_comments: This is the 3-oxoacyl-ACP reductase (FabG) step of fatty acid elongation, reducing the beta-keto group at the C18 stage. NADPH + H+ reduce 3-oxooctadecanoyl-ACP to (R)-3-hydroxyoctadecanoyl-ACP, producing NADP+. The reaction is stoichiometrically balanced (one hydride from NADPH plus one proton reduce the ketone to a hydroxyl). In vivo it proceeds in the reductive direction toward the hydroxyacyl product during fatty acid biosynthesis.

rxn01285.other_comments: This is tartrate decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.73), which converts (R,R)-tartrate to D-glycerate plus CO2. Tartrate (C4H4O6, 2- charge) + H+ yields glycerate (C3H5O4, 1- charge) + CO2. Atom balance: C 4=3+1; O 6=4+2; H tartrate 4 + 1 H+ = 5 = glycerate 5; charge: -2 +1 = -1 on left, -1 on right. The reaction is stoichiometrically balanced. Decarboxylations are essentially irreversible in vivo due to CO2 release, so the reaction proceeds in the forward direction.

rxn08179.other_comments: This is the biotin sulfoxide reductase (BisC) reaction, reducing d-biotin d-sulfoxide back to biotin (BIOT) using NADPH as the electron donor. Stoichiometry is balanced: the sulfoxide S=O oxygen is removed as water, with NADPH + H+ providing two electrons and two protons (one consumed to form water, leaving NADP+). Atoms and charges balance correctly.

errors: Reaction is written in the wrong direction relative to its stated enzymatic chemistry. The recyclizing oxidoreductase (Stizolobinate synthase) converts the ring-opened muconate semialdehyde intermediate plus NADP into Stizolobinate; as written, this consumes NADPH to open the ring, which is the reverse of the biosynthetic chemistry.

Atom/charge balance should be verified: the ring-opening/recyclization with O2 incorporation is not represented (the named enzyme is an oxygenase 'recyclizing', implying O2 involvement), so the equation as shown likely omits O2/H2O and is unbalanced for oxygen.
rxn03156.other_comments: This is the stizolobinate biosynthesis branch from L-DOPA. The intermediate 5-(L-alanin-3-yl)-2-hydroxy-cis,cis-muconate 6-semialdehyde is the ring-opened DOPA-extradiol-cleavage product, which is recyclized with reduction by NADPH to form Stizolobinate. Physiologically the flux goes toward Stizolobinate (NADPH consumed).

errors: Hydrogen/charge imbalance: the reaction as written is not properly balanced. Oxidation of a -CH2OH to a -COOH consumes 1 O2 and 1 NADPH, producing 1 H2O. The full conversion of 26-hydroxyl to 26-carboxyl (an additional 2-electron oxidation through the aldehyde) requires 2 O2 and 2 NADPH and yields 2 H2O, not 3 H2O. The water and proton stoichiometry shown (3 H2O, +H+) does not balance with 2 NADPH + 2 O2; expect 2 H2O for the two monooxygenation steps.
rxn14236.other_comments: This is a CYP27A1-type cytochrome P450 monooxygenase reaction (sterol 26/27-hydroxylase) oxidizing the C26 hydroxyl of 7alpha,26-dihydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one fully to the carboxylic acid (7alpha-hydroxy-3-oxo-4-cholestenoate) in the bile acid synthesis pathway. The two-NADPH/two-O2 stoichiometry reflects two sequential P450 oxidation steps (alcohol -> aldehyde -> acid).

rxn10951.other_comments: This represents a pyruvate dehydrogenase/oxidoreductase-type reaction where pyruvate is oxidatively decarboxylated to acetyl-CoA, with CO2 released and CoA incorporated. The electron acceptor here is FMN, reduced to FMNH2. Stoichiometry balances: carbon (3 from pyruvate = 1 CO2 + 2 in acetyl group), electrons/protons accounted for by the 2-electron, 2-proton reduction of FMN to FMNH2 (pyruvate + CoA -> acetyl-CoA + CO2 + 2H+ + 2e-; FMN + 2H+ + 2e- -> FMNH2; net consumes the H+ as shown). Charge and mass appear balanced. Oxidative decarboxylation coupled to flavin reduction is strongly exergonic and effectively irreversible in vivo.

errors: The reaction is described as a 'keto-ylation' but appears to represent a methyltransfer/methylation event (SAM to SAH conversion). The naming is inconsistent with the chemistry shown.

Mass balance is questionable: converting a C58 acyl chain to a C59 acyl chain via SAM adds one methyl group (CH2 or CH3), but the inclusion of H2O as a substrate is unusual for a simple SAM-dependent methyltransferase and suggests the atom balance is not fully accounted for.

The carbon increment (C58 to C59, +1 carbon) is consistent with a single methyl transfer from SAM, but the stoichiometry cannot be fully verified without explicit elemental formulas for the ACP-bound substrates.
Role of H2O is unclear; methyltransferases do not typically consume water, indicating a possible imbalance in protons/oxygen.
rxn13485.other_comments: This appears to be a SAM-dependent methyltransferase reaction (likely a methyl branch addition in mycolic/meromycolic acid biosynthesis given the long-chain ACP-bound substrates and the 'meroacid' nomenclature). The reaction transfers a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine, producing S-adenosyl-homocysteine and extending/modifying the acyl-ACP from C58 to C59. SAM-dependent methylations are generally thermodynamically driven forward in vivo.

errors: The reaction as written shows identical species on both sides (H+ + 4-Hydroxybutanoate <=> H+ + 4-Hydroxybutanoate) with no compartment distinction; a transport reaction requires the metabolites to be assigned to different compartments (e.g., extracellular vs cytosolic) to represent net movement across the membrane. As written, it is a null reaction with no net change.
rxn12565.other_comments: This is intended to be a proton symport transport reaction for 4-hydroxybutanoate, coupling H+ movement with the substrate across the membrane. Stoichiometry is balanced 1:1 for H+ and 4-hydroxybutanoate, which is appropriate for symport, but the lack of compartment labels makes the reaction trivial/identity as written.

rxn11741.other_comments: This reaction (R08207) represents the cytochrome P450 (psoralen synthase, CYP71AJ1) catalyzed conversion of (+)-marmesin to psoralen (Ficusin). The enzyme is a monooxygenase using NADPH and O2, cleaving the side chain of marmesin to release acetone and form the furanocoumarin psoralen. Atom and charge balance: marmesin (C14H16O4) + O2 + NADPH + H+ yields psoralen/ficusin (C11H6O3) + acetone (C3H6O) + 2 H2O + NADP+. Carbon: 14 = 11+3, balanced. The reaction is stoichiometrically consistent.

errors: The reaction as written is unbalanced and runs in the non-physiological direction for a condensation/hydrolysis pattern. As written (left to right), CoA + H+ + 3-Ethylmalate -> H2O + Glyoxylate + Butyryl-CoA: carbon balance: 3-ethylmalate (C7H10O5, as the doubly deprotonated form C7H8O5^2-) plus CoA should compare to glyoxylate (C2H1O3^-) + butyryl-CoA. Butyryl-CoA carries a 4-carbon acyl group; 3-ethylmalate (7 C) minus glyoxylate (2 C) gives a 5-carbon acyl fragment, not 4-carbon. There is a one-carbon discrepancy in the acyl portion (a 1-carboxypropyl/2-ethyl group corresponds to a C4 acid butanoyl only if the malate-side carbons are counted differently), indicating the carbon and the named '1-carboxypropyl-forming' descriptor are inconsistent with butyryl-CoA.
Charge/proton balance is questionable: consuming H+ and water while forming a free acid (glyoxylate) and a thioester needs careful reconciliation.
rxn00876.other_comments: This is the reverse of an aldol-type Claisen condensation: physiologically a butanoyl-CoA (or acyl-CoA) condenses with glyoxylate to form 3-ethylmalate (3-ethylmalyl/2-ethylmalate intermediate), releasing CoA. The EC-style name (butanoyl-CoA:glyoxylate C-butanoyltransferase, thioester-hydrolysing) describes the condensation. As written here the reaction runs in the thiolytic/cleavage direction (regenerating butyryl-CoA), which is the reverse of the biosynthetic in vivo direction. Note 'Glyoxalate' is a misspelling of glyoxylate.

rxn09127.other_comments: This is a phospholipase A1 reaction hydrolyzing the sn-1 ester bond of 1,2-dihexadec-9-enoyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate (a diacylglycerophosphate / phosphatidate with two C16:1 acyl chains). Water cleaves the sn-1 acyl group, releasing hexadecenoate (C16:1 free fatty acid) and the 2-acyl-glycerophosphate (lysophosphatidic acid), with release of a proton. The stoichiometry is mass- and charge-balanced: one acyl chain is removed from a diacyl species, leaving a monoacyl species plus the free fatty acid and H+.

rxn03561.other_comments: This is the p-cumate 2,3-dioxygenase reaction (EC 1.14.12.-), a Rieske-type aromatic ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase. p-Cumate (4-isopropylbenzoate) is converted to cis-2,3-dihydroxy-2,3-dihydro-p-cumate. Both oxygen atoms of O2 are incorporated into the dihydrodiol product, and NADH provides the reducing equivalents to regenerate the dihydrodiol. The stoichiometry is balanced: NADH + O2 + H+ + substrate -> NAD+ + cis-dihydrodiol product. This is part of the p-cumate degradation pathway (e.g., in Pseudomonas putida F1).

rxn11817.other_comments: This represents the decomposition of aldoifosfamide (4-aldophosphamide form, the open-chain aldehyde of activated ifosfamide) into isophosphoramide mustard (the active alkylating agent) and acrolein (propenal), with release of a proton. This is a beta-elimination/retro-Michael type breakdown analogous to the conversion of aldophosphamide to phosphoramide mustard plus acrolein in cyclophosphamide metabolism. Stoichiometry is balanced: aldoifosfamide fragments into the two products plus H+. In vivo this spontaneous, non-enzymatic decomposition proceeds essentially irreversibly toward formation of the cytotoxic mustard and acrolein.

rxn02332.other_comments: This is the 6-phospho-beta-galactosidase reaction (EC 3.2.1.85). Lactose-6-phosphate is hydrolyzed into D-glucose and D-galactose 6-phosphate. The reaction is mass-balanced: lactose-6-phosphate (C12H23O14P) plus water yields glucose (C6H12O6) and galactose-6-phosphate (C6H13O9P). As a hydrolysis reaction, it is thermodynamically favorable and effectively irreversible in vivo.

errors: The H+ stoichiometry is incorrect. Each condensation of IPP with the growing prenyl chain releases one PPi but does not release a proton; the correct equation should not include 8 H+. The reaction should be: 8 IPP + farnesyl-PP -> 8 PPi + undecaprenyl-PP (bactoprenyl-PP), with no protons produced.
rxn09345.other_comments: This is undecaprenyl diphosphate (cis-prenyltransferase, UppS) synthesis. Farnesyl diphosphate (C15) is extended by 8 isopentenyl diphosphate units to form the C55 undecaprenyl (bactoprenyl) diphosphate, releasing 8 PPi. The carbon count is correct: 15 + 8x5 = 55. The reaction is essentially irreversible in vivo, driven forward by PPi release/hydrolysis.

errors: Charge/proton imbalance: the reaction as written does not balance protons (H+). A typical P450 monooxygenase (CYP17A1 lyase activity) reaction is: 17alpha-Hydroxypregnenolone + NADPH + H+ + O2 -> DHEA + acetaldehyde (or acetate with additional oxidation) + NADP+ + H2O
Product identity error: the physiological lyase product is acetaldehyde, not acetate; producing acetate would require an additional oxidation step and change the redox/oxygen stoichiometry
Oxygen/redox imbalance: if acetate (more oxidized) is produced instead of acetaldehyde, the stated single O2 and single NADPH are inconsistent with the carbon-carbon cleavage stoichiometry
DHA is ambiguous notation; here it should be DHEA (dehydroepiandrosterone = 3beta-Hydroxyandrost-5-en-17-one), not dihydroxyacetone
rxn02443.other_comments: This represents the 17,20-lyase activity of CYP17A1 converting 17alpha-hydroxypregnenolone to dehydroepiandrosterone (the named 3beta-Hydroxyandrost-5-en-17-one) with cleavage of the C17-C20 side chain. It is an NADPH/O2-dependent cytochrome P450 monooxygenase reaction.

rxn04454.other_comments: This reaction represents isochorismate pyruvate-lyase (e.g., PchB in Pseudomonas), which converts isochorismate into salicylate (SALC) and pyruvate. The stoichiometry is balanced: isochorismate (C10H8O6, as the dianion) is cleaved into salicylate (C7H5O3) and pyruvate (C3H3O3), with atoms and charges conserved. The reaction is a lyase-type elimination and proceeds essentially irreversibly in the salicylate-forming direction in vivo.

errors: Substrate name lists seven oxo groups (3,5,7,9,11,13,15-Heptaoxo) but the product name '3,5,7,11,13,15-Heptaoxo-9-hydroxy' lists only six oxo positions while still calling it 'heptaoxo' - inconsistent nomenclature; the 9-position is reduced from oxo to hydroxy so the product should have six oxo groups (hexaoxo)

Redox balance: NADH reduces one keto (oxo) group to a hydroxyl, consuming NADH + H+ and producing NAD+. This is consistent with a ketoreductase step, but the naming of the product as 'heptaoxo' is contradictory with the introduction of a hydroxyl
rxn07128.other_comments: This represents a beta-ketoacyl-ACP reductase-type step reducing the 9-oxo group of a polyketo (polyketide-like) ACP intermediate to a 9-hydroxy group, oxidizing NADH to NAD+. The chemistry (one keto reduced to hydroxyl, one NADH consumed) is balanced, but the product nomenclature incorrectly retains 'heptaoxo' despite removal of one oxo group. [directionality_note] Ketoreductase steps in fatty acid/polyketide synthesis using NADH/NADPH are strongly driven toward the reduced (hydroxy) product in vivo

rxn14276.other_comments: This is a 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase reaction oxidizing the 17beta-hydroxyl group of 11beta-hydroxytestosterone to a ketone, yielding 4-androsten-11beta-ol-3,17-dione (11beta-hydroxyandrostenedione). NADP+ is reduced to NADPH + H+. The reaction is balanced: removal of two hydrogens (as hydride + proton) from the C17 hydroxyl to form the ketone matches the NADP+/NADPH+H+ couple. Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and charge balance are consistent.

errors: Product naming inconsistency: the substrate is already described as having '1 cyclopropane ring' and the product is described as 'cyclopropanated... (1 cyclopropane ring)', which fails to reflect the net addition of a new cyclopropane ring (should change from n to n+1 rings)
The SAM-dependent cyclopropanation/methylation should introduce a methylene group from SAM; the carbon mass balance is not clearly accounted for in the named metabolites
rxn10660.other_comments: This represents a SAM-dependent cyclopropane synthase (e.g., Mtb mycolic acid methyltransferases like CmaA1/CmaA2/MmaA2) reaction transferring a methylene from SAM to a double bond of a meromycolate chain on ACP, producing a cyclopropane ring and releasing SAH plus a proton. The SAM->SAH conversion and H+ release are chemically sensible, but the substrate/product ring-count labels appear contradictory.

errors: Hydrogen (H+) is not balanced: the reduction of a ketone to a secondary alcohol by NADPH consumes only 1 H+, not 2. Correct stoichiometry: Cinchoninone + NADPH + H+ -> Cinchonidine + NADP+
rxn14398.other_comments: This represents the NADPH-dependent reduction of the ketone group of cinchoninone to form the secondary alcohol cinchonidine (a Cinchona alkaloid). The 'epimerizing' designation reflects stereochemical control producing the specific epimer. Biologically, NADPH-driven ketoreductions strongly favor the reductive direction.

rxn02174.other_comments: This is the hydrolysis of D-galactono-1,4-lactone (a cyclic ester/lactone) by a lactonase, opening the ring with water to yield the linear D-galactonate plus a proton to balance the carboxylate. The reaction is stoichiometrically and charge balanced (lactone C6H10O6 + H2O -> galactonate C6H11O7- + H+). Lactone hydrolysis is thermodynamically favorable and effectively irreversible in vivo, hence forward.

rxn04067.other_comments: This is a SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase reaction (loganic acid/secologanate carboxyl methyltransferase-type). SAM donates a methyl group to the carboxylate of secologanate, producing the methyl ester secologanin and releasing S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. The reaction is balanced 1:1:1:1, with SAM losing a methyl group to become SAH, and secologanate (the carboxylic acid) gaining a methyl to become secologanin (the methyl ester).

rxn09479.other_comments: This is the acyl-CoA oxidase reaction (EC 1.3.3.6), the first step of peroxisomal beta-oxidation. Decanoyl-CoA (C10 saturated acyl-CoA) is oxidized by molecular O2 to form trans-2-decenoyl-CoA (introducing a 2,3-double bond) with reduction of O2 to H2O2. The reaction is atom and charge balanced: each side has the acyl-CoA backbone, and O2 + 2[H] from the substrate yields H2O2 plus the unsaturated product.

errors: The substrate named '1-2-sn-glycerol-3-phosphate-C16-C19' is mislabeled. CDP-diacylglycerol synthetase acts on phosphatidic acid (a diacylglycerol-3-phosphate), not on glycerol-3-phosphate. The correct substrate is 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphate (phosphatidate).

The H+ stoichiometry should be checked; the canonical reaction is CTP + phosphatidate -> CDP-diacylglycerol + PPi (the proton balance depends on protonation states, but typically the standard reaction is written without a free H+ released).
rxn13447.other_comments: This represents CDP-diacylglycerol synthetase (EC 2.7.7.41), transferring a cytidylyl group from CTP to phosphatidic acid to form CDP-diacylglycerol plus pyrophosphate. The acyl chains C16:0 and C19:0 are specified. In vivo the reaction is driven forward by the hydrolysis of PPi, making it effectively irreversible toward CDP-DAG synthesis.

rxn00936.other_comments: This is the aspartylglucosaminidase (AGA) reaction, which hydrolyzes the N-glycosylamine bond between N-acetylglucosamine and the asparagine side chain. Water + N4-(acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl)asparagine yields N-acetyl-D-glucosamine + L-asparagine. The stoichiometry is balanced (the C-N bond is cleaved with addition of water). This is a hydrolytic glycoamidase reaction in glycoprotein degradation and proceeds essentially irreversibly in the hydrolytic (forward) direction in vivo.

rxn03017.other_comments: This is a 3beta-hydroxysteroid:NADP+ oxidoreductase reaction. It oxidizes the 3beta-hydroxyl group of 5alpha-androstan-3beta,17beta-diol to a ketone, yielding androstanolone (dihydrotestosterone, DHT) plus NADPH and H+. The reaction is balanced: removal of two hydrogens (one as hydride to NADP+ forming NADPH, one as H+) converts the secondary alcohol to a ketone. Atoms and charges are balanced. In vivo, 3-keto/3-hydroxysteroid reductase (AKR1C-type) enzymes catalyze interconversion and can proceed in either direction depending on cofactor availability and substrate concentrations.

rxn01633.other_comments: This is the reaction catalyzed by 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-L-arabinonate dehydratase (EC 4.2.1.43), part of the L-arabinose degradation pathway. The substrate 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-L-arabinonate (C5H7O5-) loses water to form 2,5-dioxopentanoate (alpha-ketoglutaric semialdehyde, C5H5O4-). Stoichiometry is balanced: C5 on both sides, with H2O accounting for the difference. As a dehydratase in a catabolic degradation pathway, it proceeds in the forward (dehydration) direction in vivo.

rxn03568.other_comments: This reaction describes the oxidation of cis-2,3-dihydrodiol DDT to 2,3-dihydroxy DDT (the corresponding catechol) catalyzed by a cis-dihydrodiol dehydrogenase, with NADP+ as the electron acceptor being reduced to NADPH + H+. Stoichiometry is balanced: removal of two hydrogens (2H) from the dihydrodiol, transferred as a hydride to NADP+ (giving NADPH) plus a released proton (H+). This is a typical step in aromatic compound degradation pathways. Although written as reversible, dihydrodiol dehydrogenases strongly favor the oxidative (forward) direction toward the catechol in vivo.

errors: The product should be peroxynitrite (ONOO-), not nitrate. The reaction of NO with superoxide (O2-) forms peroxynitrite, not nitrate, as the name of the reaction indicates.
Charge imbalance: left side has NO (0) + O2- (-1) = -1; right side has H+ (+1) + nitrate (-1) = 0. The reaction is not charge balanced.
An extra H+ is generated on the product side that is not justified; the correct product peroxynitrite (ONOO-) requires no proton release.
Atom balance: nitrate (NO3-) has 3 oxygens, but reactants supply only 3 oxygens total (1 from NO + 2 from O2-); however the correct product peroxynitrite ONOO- accounts for these atoms properly.
rxn10795.other_comments: This reaction represents the spontaneous, diffusion-limited reaction of nitric oxide (NO) with superoxide (O2-). The correct product is peroxynitrite (ONOO-), as the reaction name states, not nitrate. The written products (H+ + nitrate) are incorrect; the balanced reaction is NO + O2- -> ONOO-. The reaction is essentially irreversible (forward) in vivo.

errors: Atom imbalance: Acrylamide (C3H5NO) does not equal H2O (H2O) + Vinyl cyanide/acrylonitrile (C3H3N). Left side: C3H5NO; Right side: C3H5NO actually balances for C, H, N, O. Recheck: Acrylamide C3H5NO; acrylonitrile C3H3N + H2O (H2O) = C3H5NO. The reaction is mass-balanced.

Mislabeling concern: a 'hydro-lyase' typically removes water, but the substrate acrylamide does not contain the OH/water that is eliminated in a standard dehydration; converting an amide (-CONH2) to a nitrile (-CN) is a dehydration that is chemically plausible and balanced.
rxn03680.other_comments: The reaction depicts dehydration of acrylamide to acrylonitrile (vinyl cyanide) plus water, catalyzed by a nitrile hydratase running in reverse / an aliphatic nitrile-forming lyase. Mass balance: acrylamide C3H5NO = acrylonitrile C3H3N + H2O, which is balanced. In vivo, nitrile hydratases strongly favor hydration of nitriles to amides (acrylonitrile + H2O -> acrylamide), so the biologically favored direction is the reverse of what is written.

errors: The reaction as written shows identical species (H+ and GLUM) on both sides with the same stoichiometry, resulting in no net chemical change

A proton antiport reaction requires the two species to be transported in opposite directions across a membrane, so the metabolites must be distinguished by compartment (e.g., H+[e] + GLUM[c] <=> H+[c] + GLUM[e]) to represent a meaningful transport process
Without compartment annotations, the transport mechanism (antiport) cannot be represented and the equation is trivially balanced to zero net change
rxn12526.other_comments: This is intended to be a secondary active transport reaction for D-glucosamine driven by an antiport mechanism with protons. As written, both sides are identical because compartment labels are missing. For a proton antiport, GLUM and H+ should move in opposite directions, but as named the reaction implies symport-like coupling; in either case proper extracellular/cytoplasmic tags are needed.

rxn14239.other_comments: This reaction represents the oxidation of 3beta-hydroxy-9beta-pimara-7,15-diene-19,6beta-olide to momilactone A, with NADP+ serving as the electron acceptor (reduced to NADPH). This is catalyzed by momilactone A synthase (a short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase) in the diterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthesis pathway in rice. The stoichiometry is balanced: oxidation of a secondary alcohol (3beta-OH) to a ketone removes two hydrogens, accounting for NADPH + H+. In vivo this proceeds in the oxidative (forward) direction toward momilactone A production as a defense compound.

errors: Stoichiometry is unbalanced. Ricinine (C8H8N2O2) hydrolysis at the nitrile group to a carboxylic acid requires only 1 H2O and releases NH3. With 2 H2O, the products would need an extra oxygen and two extra hydrogens. The product 3-Carboxy-4-methoxy-N-methyl-2-pyridone (C8H9NO4) accounts for addition of only one water (as the nitrile becomes COOH: C-N triple bond + 2H2O -> COOH + NH3 is one net hydration plus the nitrogen leaving). Checking atoms: Ricinine C8H8N2O2 + 2 H2O = C8H12N2O4; products NH3 + C8H9NO4 = C8H12N2O4. Atoms actually balance.
rxn02567.other_comments: This is the hydrolysis of the nitrile group of ricinine to the corresponding carboxylic acid (a pyridone carboxylic acid), releasing ammonia. Nitrile hydrolysis to carboxylic acid via amidase-type/nitrilase activity typically uses 2 H2O (nitrile -> amide -> acid) releasing NH3. The reaction is thermodynamically favorable and effectively irreversible in vivo (hydrolysis releasing NH3).

rxn01005.other_comments: This is the UDP-glucuronate pyrophosphorylase (glucuronate-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase, EC 2.7.7.44) reaction. UTP reacts with alpha-D-glucuronate 1-phosphate to form UDP-glucuronate and pyrophosphate. The stoichiometry is balanced: UTP transfers a UMP moiety to the sugar 1-phosphate, releasing PPi. Both phosphorus and charge balance. Although chemically reversible, the reaction is often driven forward (UDP-sugar synthesis) in vivo by subsequent hydrolysis of PPi by inorganic pyrophosphatase.

errors: Product should be glycochenodeoxycholate (the glycine conjugate), not chenodeoxycholate; the reaction as written removes the CoA-bound acyl group and conjugates glycine, so the amide product is glycochenodeoxycholate, not the free bile acid

Proton stoichiometry of 2.0 H+ is incorrect; conjugation of glycine to a bile acyl-CoA releases CoA-SH and forms an amide bond, typically balanced with 1 H+ (or H2O depending on representation), not 2 H+
Mass/atom imbalance: the glycine moiety is lost in the products if the output is free chenodeoxycholate rather than the glycine-conjugated bile acid
rxn03298.other_comments: This is intended to be a bile acid-CoA:amino acid N-acyltransferase (BAAT-type) reaction transferring chenodeoxycholoyl from CoA to glycine. The product name appears wrong (should be the glycine conjugate, glycochenodeoxycholate), and the substrate name 'chenodeoxyglycocholoyl-CoA' is confusingly written. In vivo this conjugation runs strongly toward amino acid conjugate formation.

rxn05106.other_comments: This is the phosphohydrolase step in the methionine salvage pathway (MTA cycle), catalyzed by E1/E2 enzymes (e.g., MtnX/MtnB-related). The substrate 2-hydroxy-3-keto-5-methylthiopentenyl-1-phosphate is hydrolyzed by water to release inorganic phosphate, yielding 1,2-dihydroxy-3-keto-5-methylthiopentene (the dehydratase/enolase-phosphatase product). The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced as written: one phosphate group transferred to water, releasing free phosphate. Hydrolysis of a phosphate ester is thermodynamically favorable and physiologically irreversible.

errors: Mass imbalance: left side has C2 H6 N1 O3 (from 3 H+, H2CO3 = H2CO3, and cyanate OCN-) versus right side C2 H3 N1 O2 (2 CO2 + NH3); hydrogen and oxygen do not balance
Charge imbalance: left side carries net +2 (3 H+ plus cyanate -1) while right side is neutral
Cyanate decarboxylase/cyanase normally uses bicarbonate (HCO3-) as cosubstrate rather than carbonic acid (H2CO3); the canonical reaction is Cyanate + HCO3- + H+ -> 2 CO2 + NH3
rxn08277.other_comments: This represents the cyanase (cyanate hydratase/decarboxylase) reaction, which converts cyanate plus bicarbonate into carbon dioxide and ammonia. As written the formula uses H2CO3 and 3 H+, which leaves the equation unbalanced in both mass (H, O) and charge. In vivo the reaction proceeds toward CO2 and ammonia release.

rxn04934.other_comments: This reaction describes the oxidation of (2R)-3-sulfolactate to 3-sulfopyruvate coupled to reduction of NAD+ to NADH. The stoichiometry is balanced: the secondary alcohol (C-OH) is oxidized to a ketone (C=O), removing 2H (2 electrons + 2 protons), which are captured as NADH + H+. Atoms balance (C, H, O, S, N, charge). This enzyme (ComC, sulfolactate dehydrogenase) is part of coenzyme M biosynthesis/sulfolactate metabolism. NAD-linked 2-hydroxyacid dehydrogenases are typically reversible, though physiological direction depends on context (often favoring NADH-driven reduction of sulfopyruvate to sulfolactate, or oxidation in degradation pathways).

rxn05310.other_comments: This is intended to be a plasma membrane nicotinate (niacin) transport reaction moving niacin between two compartments (extracellular and cytosol). Nicotinate transport across the plasma membrane is often mediated by transporters (e.g., SLC5A8 as a Na+-coupled symporter, or proton-coupled monocarboxylate-type transporters); directionality depends on the coupling mechanism and gradients. The metabolite stoichiometry (1 niacin in : 1 niacin out) is balanced, but cotransported ions are missing if it is a secondary active transport.

rxn01941.other_comments: This is the 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (15-PGDH, EC 1.1.1.141) reaction. PGF2a (prostaglandin F2alpha, the (5Z,13E)-(15S)-9alpha,11alpha,15-trihydroxyprosta-5,13-dienoate) is oxidized at the 15-hydroxyl group to the 15-keto group, with NAD+ reduced to NADH. The reaction is balanced: oxidation of a secondary alcohol to a ketone removes 2 H (one as hydride to NAD+, one as the released H+). Mass and charge balance correctly.

rxn01304.other_comments: This is the homoserine O-succinyltransferase (MetA/MetX) reaction, the first committed step in methionine biosynthesis. Succinyl-CoA transfers its succinyl group to the hydroxyl of L-homoserine, producing O-succinyl-L-homoserine and free CoA. The reaction is balanced: atoms and charges are conserved, with the succinyl moiety transferred and CoA thioester cleaved. In vivo it proceeds forward, driven by the energetically favorable cleavage of the thioester bond.

rxn00244.other_comments: This is the oxaloacetate acetylhydrolase reaction (EC 3.7.1.1), which hydrolyzes oxaloacetate into oxalate and acetate. Mass and charge balance: oxaloacetate (C4H4O5, charge -2 at physiological pH) + H2O yields oxalate (C2O4, -2) + acetate (C2H3O2, -1) + H+. Atoms: left C4H6O6, right C4H6O6; charge left -2, right -2. The reaction is balanced. As a hydrolytic C-C bond cleavage, it is essentially irreversible in vivo, proceeding in the forward direction toward oxalate and acetate.

rxn09911.other_comments: This reaction represents an ATP-dependent L-amino acid ligase forming the dipeptide Thr-Met from L-threonine and L-methionine, with hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate. The stoichiometry is balanced: peptide bond formation releases water (which is consumed in ATP hydrolysis to ADP + Pi), and one proton is released, consistent with charge and mass balance. ATP-dependent ligases of this type (e.g., RimK-type or bacterial L-amino acid ligases, EC 6.3.2.-) drive peptide synthesis thermodynamically via ATP hydrolysis, making the reaction effectively irreversible toward dipeptide formation in vivo.

rxn10290.other_comments: This reaction represents the polymerization of lipoteichoic acid (LTA) by sequential addition of 24 glycerophosphate units from CDP-glycerol onto a diglucosyl-diacylglycerol (dimyristoylglycerol) membrane anchor. Each transfer of a glycerophosphate moiety releases one CMP and one proton, so 24 CDP-glycerol yield 24 CMP and 24 H+. The stoichiometry of CDP-glycerol, CMP, and H+ is internally consistent for n=24 repeat units. The glycerophosphate carbons/phosphates are incorporated into the growing chain. The reaction is biosynthetic and effectively irreversible in vivo (CMP release coupled to chain extension), proceeding in the forward direction.

rxn03051.other_comments: This reaction represents the CYP719A-type methylenedioxy bridge formation in berberine/protoberberine alkaloid biosynthesis. In the biosynthetic direction, (S)-tetrahydrocolumbamine (a synonym/closely related to isocorypalmine, an O-methyl scopoletin-type substrate) is converted to (S)-canadine (tetrahydroberberine) by a cytochrome P450 that forms a methylenedioxy bridge, consuming NADPH and O2 and producing NADP+ and 2 H2O. As written here the equation is reversed: the forward biological direction is Isocorypalmine + NADPH + O2 + H+ -> (S)-Canadine + NADP+ + 2 H2O. The written left-to-right (canadine -> isocorypalmine) is not the physiological direction. Stoichiometry (atoms, charge, redox cofactor balance with O2/NADPH and 2 water) is consistent for a P450 monooxygenase ring-closure forming the methylenedioxy bridge.

rxn01900.other_comments: This reaction describes the interconversion of cholestenone (4-cholesten-3-one, an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone) and coprostan-3-one (5beta-cholestan-3-one, a saturated ketone) via NADP/NADPH. The reduction of the 4,5 double bond of cholestenone to give coprostan-3-one consumes NADPH, catalyzed by 3-oxo-5beta-steroid 4-dehydrogenase (5beta-reductase, AKR1D1). Atoms are balanced: removal of the C4-C5 double bond adds 2 H (one from NADPH hydride, one from H+). As written (NADP + coprostanone -> NADPH + H+ + cholestenone), the forward direction is oxidation/desaturation, which is thermodynamically and physiologically unfavorable; in vivo the dominant flux is the reductive direction (cholestenone -> coprostanone), i.e., the reverse of the written reaction.

rxn02957.other_comments: This reaction represents a deoxynucleotide monophosphate kinase activity transferring a phosphate from ATP to 5-methyl-dCMP (deoxy-5-methylcytidylate) to form 5-methyl-dCDP plus ADP. Stoichiometrically the reaction is balanced: ATP (with one phosphate transferred) yields ADP, and the monophosphate substrate gains one phosphate to become a diphosphate. The H+ is reasonable to balance charge given the proton released/consumed in phosphoryl transfer. Atoms and phosphate groups balance overall.

errors: Stoichiometric imbalance: converting naringenin (one B-ring hydroxyl) to dihydrotricetin/dihydrotricetin (3',4',5'-trihydroxy form, i.e. eriodictyol then 5,7,3',4',5'-pentahydroxyflavanone) requires addition of 2 hydroxyl groups, consuming 2 NADPH, 2 O2, 2 H+ and producing 2 H2O and 2 NADP+; the oxygen/hydrogen balance is plausible but the charge balance is off because NADP should be written as NADP+ and the proton/hydride accounting yields net charge mismatch

rxn06166.other_comments: This represents a flavonoid B-ring hydroxylation: naringenin (4'-OH) being converted to the 3',4',5'-trihydroxy flavanone (dihydrotricetin/pentahydroxyflavanone) via two NADPH/O2-dependent monooxygenase (cytochrome P450, F3'H/F3'5'H) reactions lumped together. Each hydroxylation consumes one NADPH, one O2, one H+ and releases one H2O.

rxn05486.other_comments: This is intended to be a proton symport import of N-acetyl-D-mannosamine, where a proton and the sugar are co-transported across the membrane. As written without distinct compartments it is mass- and charge-balanced but trivially null. Symport is typically driven by the proton motive force, favoring uptake (import) in vivo.

Phosphate atoms balance (1 in, 1 out); carbon balances (12 in from cellobiose-6-P, 6+6 out); the equation is stoichiometrically correct.
rxn00608.other_comments: This is the 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase (phospho-beta-glucosidase A, BglB/CelF type) reaction hydrolyzing 6-phospho-beta-D-glucosyl-(1->4)-D-glucose (cellobiose-6-phosphate) into D-glucose and D-glucose-6-phosphate. The product naming convention (which sugar retains the phosphate) is the only ambiguity; the hydrolysis itself is correctly balanced.

rxn02328.other_comments: This is the NAD+-dependent oxidation (dehydrogenation) of 7,8-dihydro-7,8-dihydroxykynurenate to 7,8-dihydroxykynurenate, part of the kynurenate degradation pathway. The cis-dihydrodiol is oxidized to the catechol, transferring a hydride to NAD+ to form NADH plus a proton. Atoms and charges balance: removal of 2 H (as H- + H+) converts the dihydrodiol to the aromatic diol. This is the standard dihydrodiol dehydrogenase step (EC 1.3.1.-) which is essentially irreversible in the catabolic direction in vivo, driven by aromatization and downstream metabolism.

rxn02773.other_comments: This is a sulfotransferase (SULT) reaction transferring the sulfo group from PAPS (3'-phosphoadenosine-5'-phosphosulfate) to a phenolic hydroxyl group of a steroid, producing the steroid O-sulfate and PAP (adenosine 3',5'-bisphosphate). The reaction is mass and charge balanced: the sulfo transfer releases one H+ upon ester bond formation. Substrates are generic ('Phenolic steroid', 'Steroid O-sulfate') so exact atom counts cannot be verified, but the conserved PAPS/PAP and sulfo-transfer portion is consistent.

rxn03336.other_comments: This is an aldehyde dehydrogenase-type reaction oxidizing 3,4-dihydroxymandelaldehyde to 3,4-dihydroxymandelic acid, with NADP+ reduced to NADPH. The stoichiometry is balanced: the aldehyde plus water is oxidized to the carboxylic acid, releasing 2 electrons and 2 protons; NADP+ accepts a hydride (H-) leaving one H+ free, consistent with the 2 H+ shown. Atom and charge balance are consistent for an oxidative aldehyde-to-acid conversion.

rxn10245.other_comments: This reaction describes a glucosyltransferase transferring a glucose moiety from UDP-glucose to a diglucosyl-dimyristoylglycerol acceptor, forming a triglucosyl product and releasing UDP. Stoichiometry is balanced: one glucosyl unit is transferred (UDP-glucose -> UDP), and the acceptor gains one glucose (di -> tri). This is part of glycoglycerolipid biosynthesis seen in certain bacteria (e.g., Acholeplasma, Mycobacteria). Glycosyltransfer reactions using UDP-sugars are thermodynamically favorable due to cleavage of the high-energy UDP-glucose bond and are generally physiologically irreversible in the biosynthetic direction.

rxn13873.other_comments: This represents a lumped acylation step in Pseudomonas aeruginosa lipid A biosynthesis, transferring two dodecanoyl (lauroyl) groups from acyl-ACP donors onto a lipid A precursor, releasing free ACP. rxn03640.other_comments: This reaction describes the intramolecular cyclization of 4-methylaminobutanal (4-methylamino-1-butanal) to form 1-methyl-1-pyrrolinium (the cyclic Schiff base / iminium ion) with release of water. The reaction is essentially balanced when accounting for the cationic product and proton bookkeeping. This is a key step in nicotine/tropane alkaloid biosynthesis.

rxn03885.other_comments: This is the mannonate dehydratase (D-mannonate hydro-lyase, EC 4.2.1.8) reaction, part of the Entner-Doudoroff-related hexuronate degradation pathway. D-mannonate is dehydrated to form 2-keto-3-deoxygluconate (2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconate) with release of water. The stoichiometry is balanced: D-mannonate (C6H12O7) yields 2-keto-3-deoxygluconate (C6H10O6) plus H2O. Atoms and charges are conserved. In vivo this dehydration is essentially irreversible and proceeds toward the keto-deoxy sugar acid.

rxn02526.other_comments: This is the benzene 1,2-dioxygenase reaction (EC 1.14.12.3), which converts benzene plus molecular oxygen plus NADH into cis-1,2-dihydrobenzene-1,2-diol (cis-benzene glycol, cis-benzene dihydrodiol) plus NAD+. Stoichiometry balances: NADH (C21H29N7O14P2) + O2 + H+ + benzene (C6H6) yields NAD+ (C21H27N7O14P2) + cis-benzeneglycol (C6H8O2). Both oxygen atoms from O2 are incorporated into the product (dioxygenase), with NADH providing the two electrons. Carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, phosphorus, and charge all balance.

rxn05109.other_comments: This reaction is catalyzed by citramalate synthase (R-citramalate synthase, EC 2.3.1.182), which condenses acetyl-CoA with pyruvate and water to form (R)-citramalate, releasing CoA and a proton. The stoichiometry is balanced: acetyl-CoA (C23) plus pyruvate (C3H3O3-) plus water yields citramalate (C5H6O5 2-) plus CoA plus H+. Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and charge balance. This is the committed first step in isoleucine biosynthesis via the citramalate pathway in some bacteria/archaea (e.g., Methanococcus, Leptospira).

rxn01674.other_comments: This reaction represents a phosphotransfer where dCTP donates a phosphate to uridine, producing UMP and dCDP, with release of a proton. Atom and charge balance: Uridine (C9H12N2O6) + dCTP (C9H12N3O13P3, charge -4) yields H+ + UMP (C9H11N2O9P, charge -2) + dCDP (C9H12N3O10P2, charge -3). Checking atoms: left C18H24N5O19P3, right H+ + UMP + dCDP = C18H24N5O19P3. Balanced. Charge: left -4, right (+1) + (-2) + (-3) = -4. Balanced. This is a kinase/phosphotransferase reaction; such phosphotransfers from a high-energy NTP to a nucleoside are thermodynamically favorable in the forward direction in vivo.

rxn04185.other_comments: This reaction represents the cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP, C20) to syn-copalyl diphosphate (syn-CPP), catalyzed by a copalyl diphosphate synthase (a class II diterpene cyclase). The reaction is an intramolecular protonation-initiated cyclization that forms the bicyclic labdane skeleton with no atoms gained or lost, so it is stoichiometrically balanced (C20H36O7P2 isomerization). In vivo this cyclization is essentially irreversible and proceeds toward the cyclized product. Note: the enzyme name listed (lyase/decyclizing) describes the reverse nomenclature convention, but the metabolic flux is GGPP -> syn-CPP.

rxn10852.other_comments: This is the 6-phospho-beta-galactosidase (LacG, EC 3.2.1.85) reaction, which hydrolyzes lactose-6-phosphate into D-glucose and D-galactose-6-phosphate. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: lactose-6-P (C12H22O14P) + H2O yields glucose (C6H12O6) + galactose-6-P (C6H11O9P). As a hydrolase reaction, it proceeds essentially irreversibly in the forward (hydrolytic) direction in vivo, following PTS-mediated uptake of lactose in many Gram-positive bacteria.

rxn11004.other_comments: The reaction depicts oxidative decarboxylation of 2-oxoglutarate (alpha-ketoglutarate) to succinate and CO2 with FAD as the electron acceptor. rxn02962.other_comments: The input describes degradation of 2-aminoethylphosphonate (ciliatine) supposedly yielding phosphate and ethanolamine (aminoethanol) with hydrogen peroxide as a co-substrate. rxn11404.other_comments: This is intended to be a proton-symport transport reaction importing methyl beta-D-galactoside from the extracellular (periplasmic) space into the cytoplasm coupled to proton movement. rxn01948.other_comments: This is the aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (DDC) reaction converting 5-hydroxy-L-tryptophan to serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine). Atoms balance: 5-hydroxy-L-tryptophan (C11H12N2O3) plus a proton yields CO2 (CO2) plus serotonin (C10H13N2O+, as cation). Carbon: 11 = 1 + 10; the decarboxylation releases the carboxyl carbon as CO2 and consumes a proton to form the protonated amine. Reaction is PLP-dependent and physiologically irreversible.

rxn06348.other_comments: This is a PTS (phosphoenolpyruvate:sugar phosphotransferase system) reaction (EC 2.7.1.202), where a phospho-histidine protein donor transfers its phosphoryl group to D-fructose, yielding D-fructose-1-phosphate and the dephosphorylated protein histidine. The stoichiometry is balanced: one phosphoryl group is transferred from the protein to the sugar. The naming convention (N-pai/N-pros referring to the tele/pros nitrogens of histidine) is consistent with phosphohistidine chemistry. In vivo, the PTS system drives concomitant sugar uptake and phosphorylation, so this transfer proceeds in the forward direction.

rxn04601.other_comments: This is the 3-(3-hydroxyphenyl)propionate 2-monooxygenase (MhpA) reaction. It hydroxylates 3-(3-hydroxyphenyl)propanoate (dihydro-3-coumaric acid) to 2,3-dihydroxyphenylpropanoate (DHPP). The reaction consumes NADH, O2, and H+, releasing water and NAD+, with one oxygen atom incorporated into the substrate. rxn00415.other_comments: This is the glutamine-pyruvate transaminase reaction (EC 2.6.1.15), also known as glutaminase-transaminase. rxn09916.other_comments: This represents an L-amino acid ligase (Lal-type) reaction forming the dipeptide Thr-Phe from L-threonine and L-phenylalanine, driven by ATP hydrolysis to ADP and inorganic phosphate. rxn10619.other_comments: This is the fumarate reductase reaction, where fumarate is reduced to succinate using menaquinol-6 as the electron donor, which is oxidized to menaquinone-6. The reaction is balanced: fumarate (C4H2O4 2-) gains 2 H to become succinate (C4H4O4 2-), and menaquinol6 (reduced) loses 2 H to become menaquinone6 (oxidized). rxn06389.other_comments: This reaction represents phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate 5-kinase (PIP5K), which transfers the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 5-position of PI(4)P to form PI(4,5)P2, releasing ADP and a proton. The stoichiometry is balanced: ATP provides the phosphate, ADP and H+ are released, consistent with a kinase reaction. The proton release reflects the net charge balance of phosphate transfer. In vivo, kinase-catalyzed phosphate transfer from ATP is strongly favored thermodynamically and proceeds in the forward (phosphorylation) direction.

rxn04142.other_comments: This is a threonine aldolase-type reaction (EC 4.1.2.5, allothreonine aldolase). L-Allothreonine is cleaved into Glycine and Acetaldehyde. PLP-dependent aldolases of this type catalyze a readily reversible aldol cleavage/condensation, so it is typically written as reversible.

rxn03605.other_comments: This is the toluene/p-cymene degradation dihydrodiol dehydrogenase step: cis-1,2-dihydroxy-4-methylcyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate is oxidatively decarboxylated and aromatized to 4-methylcatechol, reducing NADP+ to NADPH and releasing CO2. rxn04387.other_comments: This is leucoanthocyanidin reductase (LAR)-type chemistry. Resivit = leucocyanidin and Cianidanol = (+)-catechin. rxn07967.other_comments: This reaction represents 2-dehydro-D-gluconate reductase (NADH), reducing 2-dehydro-D-gluconate (2-keto-D-gluconate) to D-gluconate (GLCN) using NADH as electron donor, producing NAD+. In vivo, the favorable thermodynamics of NADH-dependent ketone reduction drive the reaction toward gluconate formation.

rxn10672.other_comments: This is phosphatidylinositol synthase (CDP-diacylglycerol-inositol 3-phosphatidyltransferase, EC 2.7.8.11). It transfers the phosphatidyl group from CDP-diacylglycerol to the hydroxyl of myo-inositol, releasing CMP and a proton and forming phosphatidylinositol (1D-myo-inositol). The substrate should strictly be myo-inositol (1D-myo-inositol); 'L-Inositol' is an imprecise/nonstandard name but interpreted here as the correct myo-inositol substrate. Stoichiometry is balanced: the phosphatidyl moiety from CDP-DAG is transferred, with CMP and H+ released. The acyl chain composition (C16:0, C19:0) is preserved between substrate and product, consistent with a transferase reaction.

rxn07679.other_comments: This is the enoyl-CoA hydratase (crotonase-type) step in jasmonate/peroxisomal beta-oxidation of OPC8-CoA. The reaction is intrinsically reversible but in vivo flux during beta-oxidation proceeds toward the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA.

rxn07484.other_comments: This is a hydrolytic dehalogenation of beta-hexachlorocyclohexane (beta-BHC, beta-lindane). Water displaces a chlorine atom yielding pentachlorocyclohexanol, plus released chloride and a proton. The reaction is balanced: beta-BHC (C6H6Cl6) + H2O yields C6H7Cl5O (pentachlorocyclohexanol) + HCl (H+ + Cl-). Atoms and charges balance correctly. This is a catabolic, essentially irreversible hydrolytic dehalogenation reaction (LinB-type haloalkane/halidohydrolase activity).

rxn01679.other_comments: This reaction describes a phosphotransferase (kinase-type) transferring a phosphate from dUTP to uridine, producing UMP and dUDP, with release of a proton. Mass balance checks out: uridine (C9H12N2O6) + dUTP (C9H15N2O14P3) gives UMP (C9H13N2O9P) + dUDP (C9H15N2O11P2) + H+. Atoms balance: C18, N4, P3, O20, and hydrogen/charge balance with the released proton. Phosphoryl transfer reactions of this type are generally thermodynamically favorable in the direction of nucleoside phosphorylation, and given the standard naming as a phosphotransferase, the forward direction is biologically favored, though such transfers can be reversible depending on cellular nucleotide pools.

rxn00098.other_comments: This reaction is the hydrolysis of adenosine 5'-tetraphosphate (Ap4, with four phosphate groups) to yield ATP and inorganic phosphate (Pi). The stoichiometry is balanced: Ap4 (C10H17N5O16P4) + H2O yields ATP (C10H16N5O13P3) + Pi (HPO4 2-/H3PO4) + H+. Charge and atom balance are consistent when accounting for the released proton. Hydrolysis of a high-energy phosphoanhydride bond is strongly exergonic and proceeds in the direction of cleavage in vivo.

rxn00793.other_comments: This is a biotin:CoA ligase (AMP-forming) reaction. ATP + CoA + biotin yields biotinyl-CoA + AMP + PPi + H+. The stoichiometry is balanced: the carboxyl group of biotin is activated via adenylation (releasing PPi), then thioesterified to CoA (releasing AMP). The single proton released is consistent with thioester formation. Such acyl-CoA synthetase (AMP-forming) reactions are thermodynamically pulled forward in vivo by the subsequent hydrolysis of pyrophosphate to two phosphates by inorganic pyrophosphatase, making the net reaction effectively irreversible toward biotinyl-CoA formation.

rxn07842.other_comments: This is the adenylate isopentenyltransferase (IPT/AMP-dependent) type reaction, EC 2.5.1.27 family. DMAPP (dimethylallyl diphosphate) transfers its dimethylallyl/isopentenyl group to the N6 position of an adenine nucleotide (here ADP), releasing pyrophosphate (PPi) and forming N6-(dimethylallyl)-ADP (isopentenyl-ADP), a cytokinin precursor. The atoms balance: the prenyl (C5H9) group transfers from DMAPP to ADP, leaving PPi and H+. In vivo this prenyl-transfer reaction is essentially irreversible because PPi is hydrolyzed by pyrophosphatases, driving the reaction forward.

rxn01829.other_comments: This is the hydrolysis of L-arabinono-1,5-lactone (a cyclic ester/lactone) to the open-chain L-arabinonate. Water is consumed and the lactone ring is opened, releasing a carboxylate group and a proton. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: left side has the lactone plus H2O; right side has L-arabinonate (carboxylate, charge -1) plus H+, balancing both atoms and charge. Lactonohydrolases typically catalyze ring opening (hydrolysis) strongly in the forward direction in vivo, as lactonization is thermodynamically unfavorable in aqueous solution.

rxn00835.other_comments: This reaction represents inosine kinase activity, transferring a phosphate from ATP to inosine to form IMP, with ADP and a proton released. The reaction is mass- and charge-balanced: ATP (-4) + inosine (0) -> ADP (-3) + H+ (+1) + IMP (-2), giving -4 on both sides. Atom balance is also correct as the phosphate group is transferred from ATP to inosine. Kinase reactions coupling ATP hydrolysis to phosphorylation are strongly favored in the forward direction in vivo.

rxn04760.other_comments: This represents the neoxanthin synthase / violaxanthin-neoxanthin conversion in the xanthophyll/ABA biosynthetic pathway. rxn05747.other_comments: This reaction represents the reduction of menaquinone-7 (a quinone, oxidized form) to menaquinol-7 (mql7, the reduced form) using NADH as the electron/hydrogen donor. The reaction is balanced: NADH + H+ provides two electrons and two protons (NADH carries a hydride plus the H+), reducing the quinone to quinol while NADH is oxidized to NAD+. Stoichiometry is correct with one NADH/H+ per menaquinone.

rxn11737.other_comments: This represents chlorophyllide a oxygenase (CAO) type monooxygenase activity, converting chlorophyllide a to 7-hydroxychlorophyllide a (an intermediate in chlorophyll b biosynthesis). The stoichiometry is balanced: NADPH + O2 + H+ donate two electrons and one oxygen atom is incorporated as the hydroxyl while the other is reduced to water, producing NADP+. Atoms and charges balance correctly for a hydroxylating monooxygenase. As an O2-dependent monooxygenase reaction, it is physiologically irreversible and proceeds in the forward (hydroxylating) direction.

rxn03649.other_comments: This is an alcohol dehydrogenase-type oxidation: 3-methylbenzyl alcohol (m-tolyl methanol) is oxidized to m-tolualdehyde (3-methylbenzaldehyde), with NAD+ reduced to NADH + H+. rxn07803.other_comments: This reaction represents a UDP-glucosyltransferase (phloretin/chalcone glucosyltransferase) transferring a glucosyl moiety from UDP-glucose to isosalipurpol (phloretin, the 2',4',6',4-tetrahydroxychalcone/dihydrochalcone) to form phlorizin chalcone (a glucoside) and releasing UDP. Glycosyltransferase reactions of this type are strongly favored in the biosynthetic (glucosylation) direction due to the high-energy UDP-sugar bond.

rxn04649.other_comments: This is a muconate cycloisomerase-type (lactonizing) reaction in the chloroaromatic degradation pathway. 2,3,5-Trichloro-cis,cis-muconate undergoes cycloisomerization with intramolecular lactonization, and the resulting unstable 2,4,5-trichloromuconolactone intermediate spontaneously dehalogenates, eliminating one chloride to form 2,5-dichloro-carboxymethylenebut-2-en-4-olide (a dienelactone). Mass and charge appear balanced: one Cl is released and the muconate is converted to the chlorinated dienelactone. In the chlorocatechol degradation pathway this proceeds in the lactonizing/dehalogenating (forward) direction.

rxn02287.other_comments: This is uroporphyrinogen III methyltransferase (SUMT, EC 2.1.1.107), which catalyzes two successive C-methylations of uroporphyrinogen III using 2 SAM to yield precorrin-2, producing 2 SAH. rxn05748.other_comments: This is the menaquinone-dependent nitrate reductase reaction (e.g., respiratory Nar). The equation shows 1 H+, nitrate, and menaquinol on the left, yielding H2O, nitrite, and menaquinone on the right. Charge and atoms balance if menaquinol carries 2 H relative to menaquinone, accounting for the proton consumed.

rxn12606.other_comments: This is a proton symport transport reaction for 1,2-propanediol, where a proton and 1,2-propanediol are co-transported across the membrane. Stoichiometrically it is balanced (1 H+ and 1 diol on each side). Symport transport reactions are typically reversible, driven by the proton motive force and substrate gradients.

rxn01179.other_comments: This is the chalcone synthase reaction (naringenin chalcone synthase, EC 2.3.1.74). rxn00591.other_comments: This is the dihydrodiol dehydrogenase / aromatizing decarboxylation step (3,5-cyclohexadiene-1,2-diol-1-carboxylate dehydrogenase, EC 1.3.1.25) converting the cis-dihydrodiol of benzoate to catechol with concomitant decarboxylation and reduction of NAD+ to NADH. rxn03278.other_comments: This is the cholesterol-5,6-epoxide hydrolase (ChEH) reaction, in which water opens the 5,6-epoxide ring of cholesterol-5beta,6beta-epoxide to yield cholestane-3beta,5alpha,6beta-triol. rxn07604.other_comments: This is a PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase reaction transferring a sulfonate group from 3'-phosphoadenosine-5'-phosphosulfate (PAPS) to the C24 hydroxyl of petromyzonol, yielding petromyzonol 24-sulfate (a lamprey pheromone/bile alcohol sulfate) and adenosine 3',5'-bisphosphate (PAP). rxn00783.other_comments: This is the KDPG-related aldolase reaction (2-dehydro-3-deoxy-6-phospho-D-galactonate aldolase, EC 4.1.2.21), cleaving 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-galactonate 6-phosphate into pyruvate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate. rxn01866.other_comments: This is the cyclamate sulfohydrolase (cyclamate sulfamatase) reaction. rxn08019.other_comments: This is the acyl-ACP synthetase reaction activating stearate (octadecanoate, ocdca, C18:0) onto acyl carrier protein. rxn08007.other_comments: This is the L,D-carboxypeptidase reaction that hydrolyzes the terminal D-alanine from the tetrapeptide L-Ala-D-Glu-meso-DAP-D-Ala of peptidoglycan, releasing free D-alanine and the tripeptide L-Ala-D-Glu-meso-DAP. rxn09151.other_comments: This is a phospholipase A2 reaction hydrolyzing the sn-2 ester bond of didodecanoyl (dilauroyl) phosphatidylethanolamine. rxn03943.other_comments: This is a SAM-dependent methyltransferase reaction in the puromycin biosynthesis pathway. rxn00516.other_comments: This reaction describes the hydrolysis of inosine 5'-tetraphosphate (Ip4) to ITP (inosine triphosphate) plus inorganic phosphate, with water as the hydrolyzing agent and release of a proton. rxn13362.other_comments: This is a transport reaction moving N,N-bisformyl-dityrosine across a membrane (e.g., between extracellular and cytosolic compartments). rxn10550.other_comments: This is a SAM-dependent methyltransferase reaction in tetrahydromethanopterin biosynthesis. Methyltransferase reactions are typically thermodynamically favorable and physiologically irreversible in the direction of methyl transfer.

rxn01455.other_comments: This is a kinase reaction transferring the gamma-phosphate of ATP to the C1 position of D-galacturonate, producing D-galacturonate 1-phosphate, ADP, and a proton. ATP-dependent kinase reactions are strongly exergonic due to phosphoanhydride bond hydrolysis and proceed in the phosphorylation direction in vivo.

rxn12187.other_comments: This is a sesquiterpene synthase (terpene cyclase) reaction. Carbon count: FPP C15 -> beta-selinene C15 + PPi (no carbon), which balances for carbon. The reaction is essentially irreversible in vivo due to the highly favorable loss of the diphosphate leaving group and product release.

rxn01458.other_comments: This is the lactonization of D-galacturonate to D-galacturonolactone (1,4-lactone), releasing water. The carboxylate group cyclizes with a hydroxyl to form the lactone ester. Such lactone/open-form interconversions are typically reversible and can occur spontaneously or be enzyme-catalyzed (aldonolactonase-type chemistry).

rxn00801.other_comments: This is the fumarylpyruvate hydrolase reaction, which hydrolytically cleaves 3-fumarylpyruvate into fumarate and pyruvate. rxn04875.other_comments: This is an epoxide hydrolase reaction where bromobenzene-2,3-oxide (an arene oxide) is hydrolyzed by water to form bromobenzene-2,3-dihydrodiol. rxn05669.other_comments: This is a proton-coupled transport reaction for L-Valine, where one H+ and one L-Valine are co-transported across a membrane (the same species appear on both sides representing different compartments). rxn01538.other_comments: This is thiamine kinase (ATP:thiamine phosphotransferase, EC 2.7.1.89), which phosphorylates free thiamine to thiamine monophosphate using ATP. rxn02686.other_comments: This reaction describes the NAD+-dependent oxidation of 5,12-dihydroxanthommatin to xanthommatin (an ommochrome pigment). As an oxidoreductase using the NAD+/NADH couple, the reaction is thermodynamically reversible and the in vivo direction depends on the cellular NAD+/NADH ratio and pigment redox state; xanthommatin and dihydroxanthommatin interconvert readily in ommochrome metabolism.

rxn06726.other_comments: This is the biotin protein ligase (holocarboxylase synthetase) reaction, attaching biotin to the apo-acetyl-CoA carboxylase via an amide bond to a lysine residue. Without explicit compartment labels in the formula, the directionality of the actual transport cannot be fully determined, but proton symporters are often thermodynamically driven by the proton motive force; the reaction is written as reversible.

rxn03603.other_comments: This is the toluate 1,2-dioxygenase reaction (KEGG R05291), part of toluene/xylene degradation. Toluate (4-methylbenzoate / p-toluic acid) is dihydroxylated by molecular O2 with NADPH as electron donor to yield the cis-dihydrodiol product (4-methyl-cis-1,2-dihydroxycyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate). The stoichiometry balances: substrate + O2 incorporates both oxygen atoms into the diol, NADPH is oxidized to NADP+, consuming the H+. As a dioxygenase reaction that irreversibly fixes O2, it proceeds in the forward (degradative) direction in vivo.
